# GCMS/eServices -Integrated Search

Q13. Will the Integrated Search impact the automated decision making? A13. The new Integrated Search functionality has no impact on the Automated Decision making process for lines of business such as the eTA and Express Entry programs. The system- based validation rules for these processes are identical to those in place prior to the introduction of this functionality.

The current known user issues related to the integrated search have been investigated and it has been determined that these issues do not impact the automated decision process such as the Auto Promote or the automated decision-making functionalities.

Q14, Why is there no CBSA Lookouts applet on the Search-Identifier screen? A14. By design, the information from partner databases (including information displayed in the CBSA Lookouts applet) has been integrated and made available in one consolidated location in GCMS. All data about a client drawn from partner databases is consolidated and appears in an integrated manner on the Search-Integrated screen. For any requests to change GCMS functionalities or design, please contact OMC, the Business owners.

Q15. Where can I find the AOC (Associations or Charocteristics) field in GCMS? A15. GCMS does not have AOC as it only existed in FOSS but previously stored AOC in FOSS can be found in the Search-Integrated > Client Details applet.

Q16. There's a checkmark in the Derogatory field in the Summary applet under the CiC Name Search but in the CIC Integrated Search Hit List, the Derogatory field remains blank. A16. The Derogatory field in the Summary applet is only an indicator to let users know that derogatory information exists in the database based on the Search Type. For example, the CBSA Lookout Search type directs users to look in the CBSA Lookout Search applet, while the CIC Name Search type directs users to look in the CIC Integrated Search Hit List.

# GCMS/eServices -Integrated Search

In the CIC Integrated Search Hit List applet, the Derogatory field only encompasses the following codes: DANGER, WANTED, REFER and PREVIOUSLY DEPORTED. The client could have

## OTHER derogatory information other than the listed above; therefore it is within the

responsibility of the officer to make the appropriate analysis by looking thoroughly into the client's file.

Q17. Is the CBSA Lookouts Hit List linked to the CIC Integrated Search Hit List? A17. No. The information found in the CBSA Lookouts Hit List is taken from an independent database. The information found in that applet might not correspond to the information found in the CIC Integrated Search Hit List. Users should be extremely diligent when scrolling and reading the information provided by ensuring that the client highlighted is the correct client you are searching for. As the two databases are different, a highlighted client in the Cic Integrated Search Hit List might not be the same client highlighted in the CBSA Lookouts Hit List.

Q18. The System no longer displays FOSS Action Codes in the CIC Integrated Search Hit List for clients who are aiready in GCMS. A18. Starting in Release 9.0.3, all clients that have been promoted into GCMS from FOSS will

## have their information transferred into GCMS and the FOSS Action Codes will no longer appear

in the Search screen. This ensures that users do not refer to outdate/point-in-time information that existed in FOSS before October 30, 2015. To import clients from FOSS please view the Online Help For more information, see To synchronize a client.

For information about how to find information in GCMS that was previously reflected by FOSS action codes, see Appendix 1.

Passport Issuance Process Cre ate and capture Application Information This function involves crèating a prospective application and inputting the Activity information from the application form including guarantor information, photos and client's preference (date of travel, service type, etc.).

Capture/Update ClientInformation This function involves creating client information including their address and the Activity 2 clients travel document and supporting identification documents. If the client is already in GCMS you will simply be updating their information.

Search This function searches for and matches up a client and their application with Activity 3 existing information in GCMS, the CI and FOSS. This is an important step in establishing whether or not they already exist in the system, which helps establish a clear history of transactions for a client.

Capturing Fees

# ActivityThe fees are processed using a different system called IPRMS. Once the fees are

processed, you will record the payment in GCMS.

Promote Client and Application At this point, client and application information are considered to be prospective. Activity 5 Authorized users must promote client and application to real before the application can be assessed. Processing of the application can only begin when an application is real. Assess Entitlement The system will conduct these checks by cross referencing information with other \Activity 6databases such as the CI. If there is an issue (hits), they will be flagged in GCMS. These issues will have to be reconciled before the application is finalized.

Finalize Application When a finai decision is made (approved, rejected, refused or withdrawn) and if Actiaity approved, the travel document is created along with observations, if required. This is used to generate and print the travel document that is later sent to the client.

Print the Travel Document Once the user is satisfied with the print preview, an image of what will appear on page 2 of the travel document, they can send the travel document record for printing through ePPS. Once the travel document is printed and finalized, the Status of the travel document record is updated to 'Authorized' and then Confirmed' in GCMS via an interface to indicate that quality control has been completed and to close the application.

Delivery of the Travel Document The final stage in the process is to manage the delivery of the travel document. MAcuvity Users are able to record the method and details of the delivery (including the tracking number) in GCMS.

# Mv6201

### INTRODUCTION

This lexicon is a job aid designed to facilitate understanding of the vocabulary of Passport Program Modernization Initiative. It is aimed at Passport Program employees of Citizenship and Immigration Canada, Service Canada and those of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development Canada.

#### The document contains four sections:

- GCMS
- Modernization
- Passport Program
- Acronyms
This job aid is an evergreen document. The e-Channel team and a sub-working group of the Change Management Working Group created the first version of the lexicon, and CIC-POC is the owner.

Should additions to the lexicon be required:

Service Canada employees: send an email to PPDS-Questions@pptc.gc.ca with the following information: the term to be added, its description and its translation.

Citizenship and Immigration employees, send an email to COP-GS-POC-SM@cic.gc.ca with the following information: the term to be added, its description and its translation.

T TERM TERMINOLOGIE DESCRIPTION TBS-Identity Standard SCT-Gestion de l'identité TBS Standard on Identity and Credential Assurance" are:

(1) TBS Identity Standard-The "Standard on Identity and Credential Assurance" which establishes the requirements for department to adopt a common methodology for assessing their identity and credential risks and for selecting appropriate controls or arrangements to mitigate those risks using a standardized assurance level framework.
(2) Identity assurance level-The level of confidence that an individual, organization or device is who or what it claims to be.
(3) Identity-A reference or designation used to distinguish a unique and particular individual, organization or device.
(4) Trusted referee confirmation-A process that relies on a trusted referee to establish a link to an individual. The trusted referee is determined by program-specific criteria. Examples of trusted referee include guarantor, notary and certified agent.
(5) Supporting evidence of identity-Evidence of identity that corroborates the foundational evidence of identity and assists in linking the identity information to an individual. It may also provide additional information such as a photo, signature or address. Examples include social insurance records; records of entitlement to travel, drive or obtain health insurance; and records of marriage, death or name change originating from a jurisdictional authority.
(6) Foundational evidence of identity-Evidence of identity that establishes core identity information such as given name(s), surname, date of birth, sex and place of birth. Examples include records of birth, immigration or citizenship from an authority with the necessary jurisdiction.
MODERNIZATION

Context-Sensitive Help To access context-sensitive online help while in GCMS, click in any view and press Ctrl + H. A window will appear displaying the GCMS online help topics related to the particular screen or view that is in focus.

Login Process To log into the GCMS training environment:

1.Launch your Internet browser.
2.Type the following in the address field and press Enter: https://gcms-training-smgc-formation.apps.ci.gc.ca/ Click English or Français.
3.
4. Enter your training user ID and password.
5.Click the arrow button or press Enter. Logging out If at any time you need to log out of GCMS, click File > Log Out on the Application Menu, or press Ctrl + Shift + X. NOTE: Do not use the X button on the top-right corner of the browser window, as it will generate user logging errors on the GCMS server. Timeouts A GCMS session is inactivated if there has not been any user input for 45 minutes. Closing GCMS Windows After you enter data in a window in GCMS, you should close the window by using the OK or Cancel button, not by clicking the X in the top right-hand corner. Prospective vs. Real Clients (IMM users) In GCMS, there are two possible states in which clients and applications can reside: Prospective and Real. Applications must always be created as Prospective before being made Real. However, new GCMS clients can be created as Real immediately, as long as a search has been performed within 24 hours.

#### Course Structure 2 of 3 2

So what will you learn today? This course will introduce you to many

### concepts about the Global Case Management System (GCMS) which

you will need to perform your job. This course is intended to provide you with a general overview and understanding of GCMS and

### provides a foundation for future training which will focus on specific

activities relating to the passport issuance process using GCMS.

At the end of this course, you will be able to:

- Identify the advantages of GCMS;
- Define common GCMS terms;
- Identify how GCMS supports the Passport Program;
- Understand how to log in and out of GCMS;
- Identify different areas on the GCMS Home page;
- Understand how to use GCMS online help;
- Describe GCMS screens, views, sub-tabs and applets;
- Define GCMS navigation tools;
- Identify GCMS icons and functions.

Transcript for the Login video

Login to GCMS

#### First we'll cover logging in.

The steps for logging in are slightly different depending on whether you log in to GCMS directly or via Citrix. Citrix is the secure remote access system that allows users who are outside of the CIC network to access GCMS. Examples include overseas CIC

#### A-2020-24143-000784

2A-2021-12699-000839

Immigration, Refugees and Citzenship Canada et Citoyenneté Canada Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act L'information divulguée en vertu de la oi sur l’accès à Finformation

users on the Department of Foreign Afairs, Trade and Development (DFATD) network and Canadian Border Services Agency (CBSA) users.

When accessing GCMS through Citrix, you must first log into Citrix.

On the Citrix Main page, open the GCMS-SMGC folder.

Then, double click on either the GCMS-SMGC icon to access the English environment or the SMGC-GCMS icon to access the French environment. The icon you choose will determine which language your browser opens in.

Once you double click on an icon, the GCMS splash screen appears. From here, the steps to log into GCMS are the same as when

## you log into GCMS not through Citrix.

If you are accessing GCMS directly within CIC's network and not through Citrix, you access the production environment URL through the internet browser Chrome. Please note that, if you use Windows 7, you will use the internet browser Internet Explorer.

You are presented with the GCMS splash screen where you can log in with the language of your choice.

Note that the GCMS French and English environments are housed on different servers and you cannot toggle between languages in a session. If you wish to change the language you are working in, you must log out of GCMS and either open the other icon on the Main page of Citrix or, if accessing GCMS directly, select the other language from the GCMS splash screen, and then log back in.

1. For today's demo, I will click English. The system displays the GCMS login page. Normally, a CIć user enters their ČIC email address in the User /D field, and the same password that they use to login to their CIC computer in the Password field. Since this is a non-production environment, I will enter a User ID (C010142) thāt logs me in as a Port of Spain immigration manager.
2. To login, click the Login arrow.

# Answers

The GCMS Toolbar Provides access to functions that apply in all GCMS screens, and contains drop-down lists and buttons/icons that allow you to navigate.

Screen Tabs Allow you to select different informations components available in GCMS-Clients. Events. Parties, etc.

Browser Toolbar Displays the GCMS URL, back and forward arrows and Refresh button.

The application Menu Provides access to the following functions: File, Edit, View, Navigate, Query. Tools and Help. and meetings.

The Edit Layout button Allows the GCMS home page to be customized.

The My Homepage area Shows activities that require action on your part, such as My Paused Tasks, My BF (Bring Forward) Activities, My Cases. My Fees, etc.

My Calendar Shows your calendar of GCMS events for the selected date, such as To Dos and meetings.

## Online help

## Now we'll cover the online help.

The online help is context sensitive step-by-step training that is integrated in GCMS.

To access the online help, press Ctrl + H anywhere in GCMS. The system displays a context sensitive online help window. In it, there are hyperlinks to step-by-step instructions for the options that the user has based on the screen that they have in focus. For instance, I have the Administration-User screen in focus, so the online help provides instructions on how to view user access roles.

To access the step-by-step instructions, click the hyperlink. A topic will display with step by step instructions and screenshots.

At anytime, if you want to access online help instructions other than the context-sensitive ones displayed, you can click the Show button in the top left hand corner of the screen to access the table of contents for the online help. The table of contents is organized into two categories; shared and user specific. Anything that is not in Immigration, Enforcement or Citizenship Specific books applies to multiple types of users, whereas, for instance, all of the content in the Enforcement Specific book only applies to CBSA users with Enforcement responsibilities.

Every time there is a GCMS release that changes existing functionality or introduces new functionality which impacts training, the online help is updated as required. A list of all of the new and updated topics is created in the Latest Updates to GCMS Online Help topic for each release.

Finally, there is a helpful search functionality to be aware of which allows users to search based on key words.

Transcript: Anything that is blue and underlined in GCMS is a hyperlink. Clicking on it will navigate you to somewhere else in the system. Right now, I'm on the Home screen, and as you can see, there are multipie applications assigned to me in the My Applications applet.

If I want to navigate to one of these applications, I just click on the hyperlink in the App # field

The system has navigated me to the IMM screen, PR sub-tab, and I have my permanent resident application in focus

Please take note of the Primary Office and Secondary Office fields, and that the Primary Office fleld has a value of 'Port of Spain' while the Secondary Office field has a value of Mexico'. I will explain the impact of these fields and values when discussing user access.

If I want to see information that is specific to the client on this application, I scroll down, and in the Clients & Partie: view, in the UCI/Party ID field, I click on the hyperlink. The UCI (Unique Client Identifier) is a unique identifier given

## to an individual dlient, and follows them throughout their interactions with CIC.

The system navigates to the Clients screen, Names view.

In the top left hand corner of the screen, notice that a threadbar has started to appear showing the history of my navigation through the various screens and views. In this instance, it contains the application number that I just navigated from. Another way of retumning to the application is to click on the threadbar.

Field Types4 of 4 Information is captured in a variety of ways in GCMS. You may already be familiar with how to input information such as drop down menus, pop up calendars, open text fields, etc. In GCMS they are called field control types. Choose the correct answer from the drop-down menu to fill in each blank in the following about field types. MVG applet allows you to enter text when the text field is white.

2. A MVG applet allows you to record multiple values for one field. The system maintains a history of all values recorded in the field. It is located to the right of the applicable fields.
3. A MVG applet provides a list of pre-defined values when you click the drop-down arrow to the right of the field.
4. A MVG applet allows you to turn on or off an option when you check a check box.
5. A MVG applet allows you to record a single value for one field. The system does not maintain a history of the values recorded in the field. It is located to the right of the field, and is represented by a magnifying glass.
6. A MVG applet assists you with calculating amounts in a field.
7. A MVG applet Vallows you to select a date. Submil

Passport Officer Course Module 1 IRIS® Introduction

# Introduction to IRIS®

The Passport Program network includes a local area network (LAN, also known under the French acronym RL: réseaux locaux) and a

### Notes

wide area network (WAN, also known under the French acronym RE: réseau étendu) that allows both desktop data and IRIS® data to be transmitted.

Each office is part of the local area network (LAN) and has a server that links all personal computers and printers in the office and connects personal computers to the wide area network (WAN).

Three major components of the computer network you should be aware of are:

1. Your personal computer
### 2. The local WIP (work in progress)

- Where the ESRFs being processed are kept.
3. The CI (Central Index) Where all travel document and system lookout files (approximately 9 million files) are kept.
## Logging Onto the Network and Launching IRIS®

Network

1. Turn on your scanner, then your monitor, and then the computer.
2. Press [Ctrl] + [Alt] + [Delete].
3. Ensure that the user ID is correct, and then type in your Microsoft Windows password. This will give you access to both the Wide Area Network and the Local Area Network.
IRIS®

1. Double-click the "Remote" folder located on the desktop with the left mouse button.
2. The contents of the Remote folder will appear. Double-click first on the folder then the IRIS® application representative of your region or section.

ASCII Codes for Letters with Accents In accordance with Chapter 2 of the Passport Policy Manual (PPM), accents will be included in Canadian travel documents only if they are recognized in one of Canada's official languages, i.e. English or French. The accents found in the list below are the only acceptable French characters to be entered in Passport Canada's travel documents.

Accents must be included in the name and/or place of birth only if the applicant has used accents on the application form. Where the place of birth is the same as any Passport Canada issuing authority, accents must be used (e.g. Montréal).

# Overview of Processing an ESRF in IRIS® Notes

1.Launch IRIS®.
2. Create a new ESRF. Press [Alt] + [S], then [N] to select "New" from the Service Request menu and initiate a new ESRF. Using the barcode scanner, enter the service request number and select [OK].
### 3. Applicant <F2> tab

Enter the applicant's personal information.

4. Form <F9> tab Scan the photo card.
5. DEC Data <F3> tab Enter the DEC information and any surname variations. Once the DEC information has been entered, press [Alt] + [Tab] to return to the "Scan Document" window and view the image of the photo. Review the scanned image, crop, then select [OK] in top right corner.
6. Complete the Form <F9> tab Scan the three pages of the application form. Enter the applicant's address(es). Enter the guarantor information. Check the "Data Capture Complete" box.
7.If required, go back to DEC Data <F3> tab and scan the DEC.
8. Supporting <F4> tab Scan in any supporting documents, if required.
9. Queries <F5> tab Searches must be launched against the Central Index and System Lookout.
10. Results <F7> tab The results of the queries must be viewed and processed.

11. Annotate <F11> tab Information regarding the new TD must be recorded in this tab (for example, Reason for Issuance, Observations, TD Type, Date Required, Date of Expiry, etc.) The status of the previous TD is updated based on the Reason for Issuance selected.

Ensure that your cash journal is open.

12. Fees <F12> tab The passport service fee is automatically generated by the system. Additional fees may be added, as required. Payment must be recorded and a receipt printed.

13. Select [OK] in bottom left corner to close and save the ESRF.

Note: If it is end of day, close and tally the cash journal.

### 2D Barcodes

Fillable PDF application forms are available to applicants on the Passport page of the Government of Canada website. When applicants fill out the PDF form on line, a 2D barcode appears in the upper right-hand corner of the application form.

This format of the passport application form is available for general applications (adults and children) and simplified renewal applications (adults).

Using the optical scanner, scan the 2D barcode. IRIS®will retrieve the information embedded in the 2D barcode and fill in most of the service request fields.

While the data is being retrieved, if you click on the [Cancel] button, the New Service Request window will reappear.

While the data is being retrieved, IRIS®will display the following message: "Please do not touch the keyboard while the system is retrieving the data from the barcode." It is important to wait until retrieval is complete before proceeding with any other data entry (do not touch the keyboard or the mouse).

The system runs four different queries.

1. Central Index The system queries the Central Index (CI), using primary and secondary data, to see if the applicant already has a travel document. Primary data: *Previous travel document
* Surname * Date of birth (including phantom date of birth, if applicable) *Surname variations * Date of birth variations *Given names and initials
Secondary data: * Sex

* Place of birth
2. System Lookout-Person The applicant's information is also checked against the System Lookout-Person list on the database.
3. System Lookout-DEC The DEC information that was entered in the DEC Data <F3> tab is checked against the System Lookout-DEC list on the database.
4.System Lookout-Guarantor The guarantor information entered in the Form <F9> tab is checked against the System Lookout-Guarantor list on the database.

Once the system has searched the CI and the three System Lookout lists, four icons appear at the bottom of the screen. If there is a hit, the system places a red check mark on the corresponding icon.

CI SL-DEC SL-SL-Person Guarantor

If a box is empty, it means that no search was done against the database (for example, if "Lack of DEC” was chosen in the DEC Data

# <F3> tab or if "Declaration in lieu of guarantor" or "Waived" was

chosen in the Form <F9> tab). A question mark signifies that the Central Index was not available.

If there is a match between the search criteria and the Central Index or one of the System Lookout entries, the Results <F7> tab automatically opens.

The hits for previous travel documents are listed in the "Selection List" section of the screen. Matches are listed by Type, Name, Place of Birth, Date of Birth, and Sex. If there is more than one hit, the TD results are listed from most recent to least recent. Supplementary Services appear in ascending order, following the TD with which they are associated.

Same Person Determination

Each time there is a matching record in our system, either a previous passport or an SL hit, (same surname AND date of birth), it is important to determine if it is the same person or not. This will ensure that a duplicate passport is not issued to an applicant in error.

Do not disregard a matching record just because of a different given name or sex than that appearing on the application you are processing. This criterion on its own is insufficient to make the "not the same person" determination.

1. You must review the previous file.
2. Once you have accessed the corresponding file on the system or received the file from microfilm you should compare at least 3 of the following elements: the photographs; names declared or surname variations on the previous application, other than the name the passport was issued in; the registration numbers of Birth Certificate or Citizenship Certificate numbēr and date of issue; the physical descriptions (eye colour and height); the residential addresses, information on page 3 and signatures; the guarantor, references and emergency contacts.
3. If you determine that it is the same person: Ask the applicant questions, as they have probably just forgotten that a valid TD still exists (mail in – Red: to ask for PPTC 203); Ask about trips that the applicant may have taken in the year the TD was issued; If the applicant cannot find the TD, they will have to submit a PPTC 203. Passport Officer Course Module 3 IRIS® Processing Data

Referring Security Files to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC)

Since July 2, 2013, the minister ofIm migration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) has been accountable for the issuance of Canadian travel documents and has the sole approval authority on all files that present risks to the Program from the perspective of program integrity, identity fraud and/or passport misuse.

These are some of the more common the files involved:

- An applicant requests a date of birth that is different from the one on his or her documentary of evidence of citizenship;
- A first-time applicant is unable to provide evidence of citizenship; A custody situation exists that meets existing criteria for a formal risk assessment; Any time there exists uncertainty in custody determination; There is a suspicion of guarantor and/or parental signature fraud; Multiple lost/damaged/mutilated documents; Approval of a second limited validity travel document (LVP) and/or subsequent LVPs (third LVP and over); System Lookout lists: A, AC, R, X, Z; C-41 files.
VStandard remarks are mandatory for all IRCC approvals, which does not prevent Service Canada employees from adding free- form remarks as required in order to properly document the file.

Consult the operational procedures found on our intranet page to learn more about referral to IRCC.

## Reason for Issuance-IRIS® Procedures

In the Query <F5> tab and the Results <F7> tab, a verification of the Central Index is done to determine whether the applicant already has a travel document. If a previous TD is found for the applicant and it is still valid, then it is important to verify its status.

It is important to always understand the reason why a passport is issued to an applicant and how the status of the previous passport is updated in the system.

## Previous passport is still valid

When the applicant has a previous passportthat is still valid and in his or her custody, it must be cancelled in the system. The TD must be marked in the Results <F7> tab. In the Annotate <F11> tab, the reason for issuance should be "Replace Cancelled TD”.

Physically cancel the previous passport booklet before giving it back to the applicant, if the applicant requests that it be returned. Add the standard remark indicating whether the TD was returned to the client or destroyed.

## 3. Previous passport is reported lost or stolen

If the previous passport is lost or stolen, that TD must be marked in the Results <F7> tab. In the Annotate <F11> tab, the reason for issuance should be "Replace

# Stolen TD" or "Replace Lost TD", depending upon the situation.

Form PPT 203 must be scanned in the Supporting <F4> tab.

If previous passport was reported lost or stolen without the applicant applying for a new travel document, a hit will appear in the Results <F7> tab. Compare what the applicant reported in the PPTC 201 with what is indicated in the PPTC 203.

The [Lost / Stolen...] button becomes active when "Replace Stolen TD” or "Replace Lost TD" is selected as the reason for issuance. Complete the date and location of the loss/theft as indicated on the PPTC 203.

Note: Service Fees $45 above and beyond the passportfee applies.

4. Previous passport is damaged or mutilated If the previous passport is mutilated or damaged, that TD must be marked in the Results <F7> tab. Choose "Replace Mutilated TD" or "Replace Damaged TD" as the reason for issuance. All mutilated or damaged travel documents must be retained and forwarded to Passport Protection. The duly completed "Declaration concerning a lost, stolen, inaccessible, damaged or foúnd Canadian travel document" (PPTC 203) must be scanned into IRIS®. For all mutilated travel documents, the entire TD must be scanned into IRIS®and the assistant manager must send an email to Passport Protection to inform them that the mutilated travel document is being forwarded to them.

#### Previous passport is spoiled

This procedures applies when:

1. There is an error on the bio-data page.
2. There is a defect in the Machine Readable Zone (quality control failure), such as a duplicate stock control number.
3. There is an error related to observations.
4. There is damage to the physical booklet (cover, laminate, binding, etc.) clearly not committed by the applicant, resulting in the travel document being considered faulty. Damaged or mutilated travel documents cannot be replaced under this procedure. In those situations, refer to section 1560 of the PPM. When in doubt, contact your Case Management Analyst (CMA).
#### 5. A photo is of dubious quality.

6. The Passport Program mistakenly changed the status.
7. There is express direction from PSDS, Finance or Passport operations senior management (exceptional situations) that has been forwarded to IRCC.
In case of doubt when determining whether the Passport Program is responsible for the error, a supervisor can contact a Data Integrity Analyst (DIA) at IRCC.CNDIFR-IDRFRC.IRCC@cic.gc.ca.

Replacement of a travel document with a faulty chip cannot be performed under this procedure.

Procedure

- Have in hand the travel document to be replaced.

Following a IRCC recommendation, "duplicate"should not be selected as the reason for issuance when issuing a second valid passport because this autom atically changes the status of the previous passport to "held in safekeeping", which is not correct.

By selecting "new" as the reason for issuance, the status of the previous passport stays as "in custody of applicant"and an alert is automatically generated. The alert is then verified by a Data Integrity Analyst (DIA), who ensures that the appropriate IRCC approval has been granted for the duplicate issuance and that the client has provided the necessary information.

The "suspended" status is used when a travel document is suspended in accordance with the Family Orders and Agreements Enforcement Assistance Act. This status is used when the Passport Program has requested the return of the TD, but the TD has not been received.

SL-Person or not.

2. Do not mark the TD in IRIS®.
3. Enter remarks in <F11> indicating the TD is on file (indicate all SL hits as per usual).
4. Routethe ESRF to security review and refer the file to IRCC.
5. Retain the TD on file pending clearance from the IRCC.
6. Do not physically cancel or mark the TD until advised how to proceed by IRCC.
10. PROP The "PROP" (pending return of passport) status is used when The Passport Program requests the return of a TD in accordance with section 11 of the Canadian Passport Order.
1. TD status is "PROP": refer the file to IRCC, whether the applicant is on the SL-Person or not.
2. Do not mark the TD in IRIS®.
3. Enter remarks in <F11> indicating the TD is on file (indicate all SL hits as per usual).
4. Route the ESRF to security review and refer the file to IRCC.
5. Retain the TD on file pending clearance from IRCC.

## Limited Validity Passport (LVP)

Issuance of an LVP will be considered only in the following cases: A valid passportis a residency requirement (outside Canada) or The applicant submits proof of imminent travel: airline, bus, train or boat ticket; o travel itinerary that shows proof of payment; o a statement, if travelling by car (validation of the statement is at the discretion of the passport officer, e.g. submission of proof of payment).

## Document the file

In the Supporting <F4> tab in IRIS®, scan all documentation supporting the LVP application that is not detailed on the passport application form. For example: 0Proof of travel; Signed form PPTC 116;

# o Form PPTC 117, wherein IRCC confirms the applicant's Canadian

citizenship;

# IRCC receipt for payment for a new citizenship certificate (Internet

receipt); o Statement; All other documentation relevant to the application. Annotate the file to include any pertinent information (remarks).

The decision to issue an LVP to an applicant with an acceptable passport history rests with Service Canada. Issuance of an LVP to an applicant without an acceptable passport history, as well as a second LVP or any subsequent LVP, must be approved by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).

Standard remarks sC

- For a first LVP approved by IRCC: File referred to IRCC for approval For a first LVP approved by SC: 1st LVP approved for issuance due to acceptable passport history For à second or subsequent LVP approved by IRCC: File referred to IRCC for approval
Consult the operational procedures found on our intranet page to learn more about issuing a limited validity passport.

## Passport Care

Multiple incident (MI) files can be detected in three ways:

1. After querying the system, you obtain a hit for an already existing MI file for the applicant.
2. An applicant with an LVP, which was limited because of multiple incidents related to lost, stolen, damaged, mutilated, destroyed by PPTC or found travel documents, is requesting the replacement of that LVP. An OBS 47, RE4 or CE4 is already in the travel document and you obtain an SL hit after querying the system.
3. The ĊI query results show that a travel document was issued to replace a previous valid travel document that was reported lost, stolen, damaged, mutilated, destroyed by PPTC or found. (You will find that information by looking at the WYSIWYG images of the previous travel document, which also show the status of the previous travel document.) This replacement travel document is now being reported lost, stolen, damaged, mutilated, destroyed by PPTC or found. This is considered a new MI file, since the replacement travel document is the second travel document reported lost, stolen, damaged, mutilated, destroyed by PPTC or found while still valid and a new MI file will need to be created.
If you determine that it is NOT the same person

1. Add a remark to the file indicating that it is not the same person. If you determine that it is the same person
1. Ensure that the file is properly completed, except for the Annotate <F11> tab.
2. In the Supporting <F4> tab, scan form PPTC 203 completed by the applicant.
3. Obtain proof of travel and scan it the Supporting <F4> tab.
4. Conduct the guarantor check.
5. Document the file (remarks) in the Annotate <F11> tab.
6. Forward the file to IRCC.
7. Add standard remark: "File referred to IRCC for approval"

## Notes

Once it has been determined that the applicant meets all of the simplified renewal eligibility criteria, the application may be processed.

Due to system limitations, simplified renewal applications must be completed in a specific workflow in IRIS®. When this workflow is not followed, IRIS®does not save the DEC information and any surname variations from the previous file may not be carried over, or may be truncated.

The minimum steps required before saving a file are:

F5 - Enter Stock Control number and run Queries F7 - Select record, mark and accept F2 - Verify there are no truncations in names and place of birth (POB)

- F3 - Retrieve DEC information
After the DEC data has been retrieved in F3, the file can be saved by either going into F12 or closing the file. The user CANNoT enter F12 or close the file prior to entering F3 or the problem will occur.

Processing simplified renewal applications in IRIS®basically involves electronically retrieving information from a previous ESRF to process the new record, without modifying the information.

Except for the specific scenarios outlined in the Eligibility Criteria module, passport officers are not to modify the information being retrieved.

NOTE: Applications submitted with 2D barcodes are to be used with renewal applications, where applicable. When processing an application with a barcode, you must ensure the keyboard language is the same as that of the applicant. You may use ALT-SHIFT to change the language as needed.

Although DEC and ID are not required, if presented, they must be scanned in the appropriate tab.

# Processing Fees for the replacement of Lost or Stolen

The IRIS system will automatically generate a C$45 administrative service fee in the Fees <F12> tab in addition to the travel document service fee when the

Exception: If the TD type is eDiplomatic, eSpecial, eTaiwan, or eNon-Canadian,

If a travel document was previously reported lost or stolen but has since been found and is in Passport Canada or the applicant's possession, there will be no administrative service charge. The C$45 fee will only be charged if there is need to replace a travel document that is still lost or stolen. If a client requests details concerning the circumstances in which the TD was found, advise them to make an Access to Information and Privacy request.

s.16(1)(b)
Additional information

s.16(1)(c)
Authority to produce certified true copies In the context of this procedure, certification of a Canadian travel document is exclusive to the Passport Program. While other individuals may be authorized to produce certified copies and to charge a fee for that service, e.g. lawyers, members of judiciary, chartered accountants, funeral directors, actuaries, bank managers, this procedure refers to an explicit request that the Canadian travel document be certified by a legitimate Canadian travel document issuing authority. It is the responsibility of the bearer of the travel document to determine the appropriate certifier and to pay the applicable fee.

Passport Program dry seal The Passport Program dry seal is a national security asset classified at the SECRET level, based on the expected injury to the national interest should it be compromised.

Certification authorization The certification of a travel document carries distinct responsibilities; it is therefore important that the manager (or their delegate) perform step 4 indicated in the procedure to underscore that all duties associated with the actual certification of the document are to be carried out by the same individual. This will ensure that the travel document was seen and confirm that any prepared copy is a true copy of the travel document.

Requests submitted by mail to a processing centre may require a call to:

1) Confirm the identity of the applicant.
2) Confirm that the applicant is the person making the request.
# 3) Confirm the number of copies to be produced.

4) Obtain supplementary identification (faxed copies are acceptable).
## 5) Obtain a signed request PPTC 516.

# Assigning an ESRF

Assigning an ESRF to an existing box

## There are two options:

Option 1 Open the ESRF in question, then select the Assign ESRF option from the Boxes menu. The "Reassign ESRF(s)" screen appears. Enter the number of the box you wish to assign the ESRF to and select [OK]. Reassign ESRF(ε) Box Current Values oK Location: Cancel Sub-location: Box ID: Reassign ESRF(s) to Location Sub-location G Box1D RA1234

Option 2 If you wish to assign multiple ESRFs to a box, you may open the box you wish to assign the ESRFs to. To retrieve an existing box, simply select Open Box from the Boxes menu and type in the required box number. Once you tab out of the "Box ID" field, the list of ESRFs included in the requested box, if any, appears. Keep the box open. Any ESRFs that are created or opened and are not already assigned to a box will be automatically assigned to the open box when they are saved.

BFs can be used as reminders that pop up each time you enter IRIS®. They can be created when other actions must be taken by the user. The BF can be attached to either a User ID or an ESRF.

The Guarantor Did Not Meet One of the Eligibility Criteria:

# Main Procedure for Analyzing the Eligibility Report

This procedure describes how the employee of Passport Canada will retrieve and take action on the information provided by the Guarantor Validity and Eligibility Report.

Pre-conditions:

- An Overnight Report has been created and saved on the WIP IRIS® shared drive of each Issuing Authority;
- The selected employees of Passport Canada have printed the Overnight Report.
1. Use the "Applicant information" section of the Guarantor Validity and Eligibility Report to locate all the ESRFs presented on the report.
2.For each ESRF, verify whether a data entry error has occurred in the "TD Number", "Surname" or "Date of Birth" fields. Steps to confirm data:
- Open the ESRF.
- Click on the <F9> tab.
- Click on the "Guarantor" tab.
- Using the image of the form displayed in the window of the "guarantor" section and the content of mandatory fields, compare the information to ensure no error has been made.
3. When no data entry error is detected, confirm the information provided in the "Eligibility" section of the report.
4. If, according to the report, a guarantor has failed to meet one of the eligibility criteria (see below), bring the ESRF back into the "examination" state, open the ESRF and add the remark: "G not eligible: reason". Eligibility criteria:
- Guarantor must hold a Canadian passport valid for five years*.
- Guarantor must hold a valid passport (i.e. a passport whose status is “in custody of applicant", "cancelled" or "replaced by renewal") or one that has been expired for less than one year.

# The Guarantor's Travel Document Was Not Initially Issued

for a Five-Year Validity Period but Was Extended to Its Full

# Validity:

During the eligibility verification process, the system will confirm whether the guarantor's travel document has been issued for the five-year validity period. If the travel document was initially issued for a shorter period, the Guarantor Validity and Eligibility Report will confirm the "failed" status under the "Validity" column, even if the travel document has been extended to its full validity.

Alternate Procedure for Analyzing the Eligibility Report

1. Confirm whether the TD number or stock control number (SCN) begins with DE, DC, ST or SC or with SAA or DAA. If this is the case and the guarantor meets all other eligibility criteria, the guarantor can be accepted since the travel document is a diplomatic or special passport. Under the new Guarantor Policy, these types of passport are admissible regardless of the limited validity period.

The Guarantor's Travel Document Is a Certificate of Identity, a Refugee Travel Document or a Non-Canadian Diplomatic Passport Currently, the Guarantor Policy only applies to Canadians who hold a Canadian passport. When the system has identified that a guarantor does not hold an admissible travel document, the Guarantor Validity and Eligibility Report will confirm the "failed" status under the "TD Type" column of the "Data Validity" section. The passport

Alternate procedure to step 3 of the main procedure:

1. When the system indicates that the TD type is wrong, verify the type of travel document held by the guarantor by looking at the "Guarantor" section of the report.
2. Bring the ESRF back into the "examination" state, open the ESRF and add the observation: "G not eligible: reason".
3. Go to F11 and check the "Pending" box.
4. The ESRF is sent to the Guarantor Verification Section, which will call the guarantor and the applicant to convey the pertinent information.

Passport Issuance Process Create and capture Application Information This function involves creating a prospective application and inputting the Activity information from the application form including guarantor information, photos and client's preference (date of travel, service type, etc.).

Capture/Update ClientInformation This function involves creating client information including their address and the Activity clients travel document and supporting identification documents. If the client is already in GCMS you will simply be updating their information.

Search This function searches for and matches up a client and their application with Activity 3 existing information in GCMS, the CI and FOSS. This is an important step in establishing whether or not they already exist in the system, which helps establish a clear history of transactions for a client.

Capturing Fees Activity The fees are processed using a different system called IPRMS. Once the fees are processed, you will record the payment in GCMS.

Promote Client and Application At this point, client and application information are considered to be prospective. Activity 5 Authorized users must promote client and application to real before the application can be assessed. Processing of the application can only begin when an application is real. Assess Entitlement The system will conduct these checks by cross referencing information with other 6databases such as the CI. If there is an issue (hits), they will be flagged in GCMS. These issues will have to be reconciled before the application is finalized.

Finalize Application When a finai decision is made (approved, rejected, refused or withdrawn) and if Actiaity approved, the travel document is created along with observations, if required. This is used to generate and print the travel document that is later sent to the client.

Print the Travel Document Once the user is satisfied with the print preview, an image of what will appear on page 2 of the travel document, they can send the travel document record for printing through ePPS. Once the travel document is printed and finalized, the Status of the travel document record is updated to Authorized' and then 'Confirmed' in GCMS via an interface to indicate that quality control has been completed and to close the application. Deliv ery of the Travel Document The final stage in the process is to manage the delivery of the travel document. MAcuvity Users are able to record the method and details of the delivery (including the tracking number) in GCMS.

# Mv6201

#### INTRODUCTION

This lexicon is a job aid designed to facilitate understanding of the vocabulary of Passport Program Modernization Initiative. It is aimed at Passport Program employees of Citizenship and Immigration Canada, Service Canada and those of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development Canada.

##### The document contains four sections:

- GCMS
- Modernization
- Passport Program
- Acronyms
This job aid is an evergreen document. The e-Channel team and a sub-working group of the Change Management Working Group created the first version of the lexicon, and CIC-POC is the owner.

Should additions to the lexicon be required:

Service Canada employees: send an email to PPDS-Questions@pptc.gc.ca with the following information: the term to be added, its description and its translation.

Citizenship and Immigration employees, send an email to COP-GS-POC-SM@cic.gc.ca with the following information: the term to be added, its description and its translation.

T TERM TERMINOLOGIE DESCRIPTION TBS-Identity Standard SCT-Gestion de l'identité TBS Standard on Identity and Credential Assurance" are:

(1) TBS Identity Standard-The "Standard on Identity and Credential Assurance" which establishes the requirements for department to adopt a common methodology for assessing their identity and credential risks and for selecting appropriate controls or arrangements to mitigate those risks using a standardized assurance level framework.
(2) Identity assurance level-The level of confidence that an individual, organization or device is who or what it claims to be.
(3) Identity-A reference or designation used to distinguish a unique and particular individual, organization or device.
(4) Trusted referee confirmation-A process that relies on a trusted referee to establish a link to an individual. The trusted referee is determined by program-specific criteria. Examples of trusted referee include guarantor, notary and certified agent.
(5) Supporting evidence of identity-Evidence of identity that corroborates the foundational evidence of identity and assists in linking the identity information to an individual. It may also provide additional information such as a photo, signature or address. Examples include social insurance records; records of entitlement to travel, drive or obtain health insurance; and records of marriage, death or name change originating from a jurisdictional authority.
(6) Foundational evidence of identity-Evidence of identity that establishes core identity information such as given name(s), surname, date of birth, sex and place of birth. Examples include records of birth, immigration or citizenship from an authority with the necessary jurisdiction.

Login Process To log into the GCMS training environment:

1.Launch your Internet browser. Type the following in the address field and press Enter:
2. [https://gcms-training-smgc-formation.apps.ci.gc.ca/](https://gcms-training-smgc-formation.apps.ci.gc.ca/) Click English or Français.
3.
4. Enter your training user ID and password.
5. Click the arrow button or press Enter. Logging out If at any time you need to log out of GCMS, click File > Log Out on the Application Menu, or press Ctrl + Shift + X. NOTE: Do not use the X button on the top-right corner of the browser window, as it will generate user logging errors on the GCMS server. Timeouts A GCMS session is inactivated if there has not been any user input for 45 minutes. Closing GCMS Windows After you enter data in a window in GCMS, you should close the window by using the OK or Cancel button, not by clicking the X in the top right-hand corner. Prospective vs. Real Clients (IMM users) In GCMS, there are two possible states in which clients and applications can reside: Prospective and Real. Applications must always be created as Prospective before being made Real. However, new GCMS clients can be created as Real immediately, as long as a search has been performed within 24 hours.

Introduction

## About this training workbook

This training workbook is intended for GCMS users who do not have a lot of previous experience working in GCMS. It provides a structured introduction to GCMS, including hands-on practice using GCMS navigation and search procedures. Review questions and scenarios will help you apply the knowledge you gain during each lesson.

You will need access to the GCMS training environment in order to complete this workbook. Your GCMS Manager will ensure this access is set up for you, to help you work through this document.

Through this workbook, read only users will be introduced to GCMS. Users with

# write access who are not all that familiar with GCMS will start their learning

experience here – with other training materials to follow.

This workbook is intended for all new GCMS users.

# NOTE: As indicated throughout this workbook, some exercises apply only to

certain user groups. Unless otherwise specified, complete the exercises as presented.

:Workb-tting Ste --GCMS

Workbook learning objectives After completing this workbook, you will be able to:

- Identify the different areas on the GCMS home page;
- Define GCMS terms;
- Identify GCMS icons and functions;
- Describe and use GCMS screens, views and applets;
- Use GCMS online help;
- Describe and use GCMS navigation tools; and
- Describe and use GCMS search functionality. NOTE: The GCMS quick reference sheet in Appendix A provides an “at a glance" reminder of the topics covered in this training workbook. You are encouraged to use the quick reference sheet during and after this training. How to use this workbook Sequence The first lesson is the foundation for the lessons that follow. Complete the first lesson before attempting the other lessons or exercises. Timing Complete the exercises at your own pace. We have estimated the time that may be needed for each exercise or lesson to help you plan time for training. Online help The GCMS online help is accessible from the training environment and provides step-by-step directions to help you complete this workbook. Lesson 1 contains instructions for accessing online help.

# Lesson 2: Navigating GCMS

Introduction In this lesson you will learn the basics of navigation in GCMS. Using GCMS you wil complete some exercises to apply what you learn.

# Learning objectives

At the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

- Describe GCMS screen hierarchy;
- Identify GCMS navigation tools; and
- Use GCMS navigation tools to explore GCMS. Estimated lesson duration This lesson is expected to take one hour to complete.
# Lesson 2 intended audiences

This lesson is intended for all GCMS users.

GCMS screen hierarchy GCMS uses a hierarchy of screens and views to organize and present information (see Figure 8):

- Screens (A) are located at the top of the display.
- Views (B) are located directly below the screens.
- Applets (C) within a view are located at the bottom of the display and are connected to the specific screen or view in focus. Sub-tabs allow information related within a screen or view to be organized in more detailed sections. In the example below, the PR sub-tab is selected within the IMM screen.
: Workb-tting Sta --. GCMS 2A-2021-12699-001325

Navig MS

Refer to Figure 8 as you review the GCMS definitions below.

A) Screens A screen acts as a first filter on the information, for example:
- The Clients screen displays client information,
- The Search screen displays search information. The naming convention for a screen is the name on the tab plus the word 'screen’. Examples include the Clients screen, and the Events screen. Figure 8 (A) displays the IMM-PR screen.
B) Views A view shows additional details about the selected screen. For example, the Clients screen displays information about a client. The view tabs within the Clients screen organize client data into categories, such as the client's addresses, names and documents. The naming convention for a view begins with the name of the screen that the view is attached to, followed by the name of the view, then the word 'view'. In
Figure 8 (B), the name of the view is IMM-PR > Clients and Parties view.

C) Applets An applet shows additional information about a record contained in a view. Applets exist only in certain views. An applet can either be a list or a form, and it displays specific information for the selected view. For more information about forms and lists, see the next page.
Figure 8 (C) shows the Client Details applet within the IMM-PR > Clients and
 Parties view. NOTE: When referring to screen captures in GCMS training materials you will see the combination of a screen, view and applet referred to as a view. Figure 8 for example, including screen, view and applet, will be referred to as the IMM-PR > Clients and Parties-Client Details view.

In (A) the record entries are displayed as a form, where information is located in various fields. The form provides additional details about a single record. In (B), information is presented in a list format. Information is located in a series of rows and columns. Each row represents a separate record. You can select a record by clicking anywhere on on the record. NOTE: If you click on a hyperlink (text that is blue and underlined) in a record, it will navigate you somewhere else.

# Navigation tools

This section provides a description of GCMS navigation tools, as well as some practice exercises. There are various ways to navigate within GCMS. There are six types of navigation tools:

- Tabs
- Internet Browser
- Hyperlinks
- Thread bar
- GCMS site map
- Other navigation tools
:Workb-tting Sta -. GCMS 2A-2021-12699-001332

# 1. Tabs

## Screen tabs are located just below the GCMS application menu. Each screen tab

represents the information component available in GCMS. Some screen tabs have associated sub-screen tabs (see Figure 10).

## View tabs are always displayed underneath screens. The view tabs that are

displayed differ depending on the screen tab selected above.

NOTE: For some screens, in order to access the associated views, a user must click

## on the ID hyperlink.

You can access a new tab by clicking on it. The color of the tab changes to black to

# indicate that it has been selected. When you navigate from screen to screen using

tabs, you lose the thread, or the data you were working with.

Figure 10 – Tabs

The Tab drop-down arrow provides access Screen tabs provide access to screens. to additional screens.

Screen sub-tabs provide access to specific options within screens.

View tabs provide access to views. The view tabs that are displayed differ depending on the screen tab selected and user permissions.

3. Hyperlinks Hyperlinks are displayed in blue font and become underlined when you hover your mouse over them. Clicking on hyperlinks takes you to the selected item and is the best way to navigate through GCMS. Many GCMS identifiers, such as the Unique Client Identifier (UCI), Case ID / Application ID #, File ID, Event ID, Document ID, or Medical Address ID are hyperlinked to let you navigate quickly and directly to the information associated with these identifiers.

# Field TypeDescription

### 1. MVG AppletAn MVG is a Multi Value Group. This allows you to

record multiple values for one field. The system maintains a history of all values recorded in the field. It is located to the right of the applicable fields.

### 2. Calculator Opens a calculator to assist you with calculating

amounts.

### 3. Check Box Allows you to turn on or off an option when you

check a check box.

### 4. Calendar Enables you to select a date from a calendar. It is

located to the right of the applicable fields.

## 5. Pick AppletOpens a window to select from a list of values.

## 6.Drop-down List Provides a list of pre-defined values when you click

the drop-down arrow to the right of the field.

### 7. Open TextAllows you to enter text when the field is white.

### Finding Clients in GCMS

A client is a person who has submitted an application for a CIC service, or who is subject to enforcement action.

There are two ways to search for clients in GCMS. One is by conducting a name search and the other is by conducting a search using a specific identifier such as a

# Unique Client Identifier (UCI). Use of Identifier search should be limited to

retrieving a known client.

## The exercises that follow provide you with an opportunity to practice finding

clients in GCMS. Remember, you have ready access to the GCMS online help feature to assist you in completing these exercises.

### Search Person

When conducting a name search, users can search for multiple persons at the

## same time and can navigate from one result to the next without losing the

entered search criteria.

The best method to search for a client when you do not know if the client exists in FOSS/GCMS is to conduct a name search.

NOTE: Information from both GCMS and FOSS is displayed in a single result. User access determines who can see FOSS information.

## Search by Employment Validation

GCMS allows users to search the ESDC (Economic and Social Development Canada) database for employment validation information. There are two ways to search for employment validation records:

- By conducting a name search; and
- By conducting a search using a specific ESDC file number. The steps to search for employment validation information are described in the Search Screen > Searching by ESDC section of GCMS online help.

### Search by eDocs

GCMS allows all users to search for and view documents which are saved in the e- Storage repository.

The steps to search for documents stored in e-Storage using the eDocs sub-tab are described in the Search Screen > Searching by eDocs >To search using eDocs

## section of GCMS online help.

## Search by CAIPS

CAIPS was the system that was used prior to GCMS to process immigration

# applications overseas. CAIPS has been decommissioned and is now used as a

# database. Users are able to search for applications and information in CAIPS using

GCMS.

The steps to search for applications in CAIPS using the CAIPS sub-tab are described in the Search Screen > Searching by CAIPS >To search by CAIPS section of GCMS online help.

### Search by IBAS/LSFD

IBAS /LSFD (Integrated Border Alerting Service/Lost, Stolen or Fradulent Document) searches allow users to search for immigration lookouts and LSFD documents in FOSS. The search is based on document number and/or serial number and the Country of Issue. The searches are executed individually and the results combined into a single hit list.

## Querying vs. Searching in GCMS

Querying is a different concept in GCMS. Once a person has verified a client's identity in the system by performing a search, and has a unique identifier that belongs to the client, they can query for them instead of searching.

A query is used to retrieve all records that meet certain criteria. A variety of queries can be run on a regular basis to manage your inventory, track volumes or identify applications for follow up. Queries can be run in any GCMS screen. You can also run a query within a view of a particular record.

The steps to initiate queries in GCMS are described in the Queries section of GCMS online help.

Activity 1: Create and capture Application Information This function involves creating a prospective application and inputting the information from the application form including guarantor, photos and client's preference (date of travel, service type, etc.). Activity 2: Capture/Update Client Information This function involves creating client information including their address and the clients travel document and supporting identification documents. If the client is already in GCMS you will simply be updating their information. Activity 3: Search This function searches for and matches up a client and their application with existing information in GCMS, the Central Index (CI) and Field Operations Support System (FOSS). This is an important step in establishing whether or not they already exist in the system, which helps establish a clear historyof transactions for a client.

### Activity 4: Capturing Fees

## Activity 6: Assess Entitlement

The system will conduct these checks by cross referencing information with other databases such as the Cl. If there is an issue (hits), they will be flagged in GCMS. These issues will have to be reconciled before the application is finalized.

## Activity 7: Finalize Application

When a final decision is made (approved, rejected, refused or withdrawn) and if approved, the travel document is created along with observations, if required. This is used to generate and print the travel document that is later sent to the client.

## Activity 8: Print the Travel Document

Once the user is satisfied with the print preview, an image of what will appear on page 2 of the travel document, they can send the travel document record for printing through ePPS. Once the travel document is printed and finalized, the Status of the travel document record is updated to 'Authorized' and then ‘Confirmed’ in GCMS via an interface to indicate that quality control has been completed and to close the application.

Activity 9: Delivery of the Travel Document

The final stage in the process is to manage the delivery of the travel document. Users are able to record the method and details of the delivery (including the tracking number) in GCMS.

### Online help – Transcript:

### Now we'll cover the online help.

The online help is context sensitive step-by-step training that is integrated in GCMS.

To access the online help, press Ctrl + H anywhere in GCMS. The system displays a context sensitive online help window. In it, there are hyperlinks to step-by-step instructions for the options that the user has based on the screen that they have in focus. For instance, I have the Administration-User screen in focus, so the online help provides instructions on how to view user access roles.

To access the step-by-step instructions, click the hyperlink. A topic will display with step by step instructions and screenshots.

At anytime, if you want to access online help instructions other than the context-sensitive ones displayed, you can click the Show button in the top left hand corner of the screen to access the table of contents for the online help. The table of contents is organized into two categories; shared and user specific. Anything that is not in Immigration, Enforcement or Citizenship Specific books applies to multiple types of users, whereas, for instance, all of the content in the Enforcement Specific book only applies to CBSA users with Enforcement responsibilities.

Screens are located at the top of the display. A screen acts as a first filter on the information, for example:

The Clients screen displays client information.

### The Search screen displays search information.

The naming convention for a screen is the name on the tab plus the word `screen'. For

### example, the Clients screen.

Views are located directly below the screens, and views show additional details about the selected screen. For example, the Clients screen displays information about a client. The view tabs within the Clients screen organize client data into categories, such as the client's

### address, name and documents.

Hgasetie fefyeees artenRefyies aedaefCByAa

The naming convention for a view begins with the name of the screen that the view is attached to, followed by the name of the view, then the word 'view'. For example, the Clients > Names view.

Sub tabs are located on certain screens and views, and are a method of subdividing information. For example, the Clients > Documents view has the following sub-tabs; Travel Documents, ID Supporting Documents, CIC Documents, and ID Supporting Documents CIT.

The naming convention for a sub-tab varies depending on whether it is located on a screen or a view. If it is on a screen, it begins with the name of the screen that the sub-tab is attached to, followed by the name of the sub-tab, then the word 'screen'. For example, the IMM – PR screen. If it is on a view, it begins with the name of the screen that the view is attached to, followed by the name of the view, followed by the name of the sub-tab, then the word 'view'.

For example, the Clients > Documents – Travel Documents view.

Applets within a view are located at the bottom of the display and are connected to the

# specific screen or view infocus. An applet shows additional information about a record

contained in a view. Applets exist only in certain views.

An applet can either be a list (results from a Search) or a form (Client Details) and it displays specific information for the selected view (or sub-tab if applicable).

### Screen Hierarchy – Transcript

At the top of the screen, there are tabs that look like tabs on a binder. These are called screen tabs. Each screen tab allows the user to access a different screen containing specific types of information, activities or applications. For instance, clicking on the CIT screen tab will allow a user to query for and process a citizenship application, whereas the IMM screen tab will allow a user to query for and process an immigration application.

I'm going to click on the Clients screen tab.

A client refers to an individual person. A key concept of GCMS is that a client must exist in order to create any type of application or activity related to services provided to the client. As you can see, there are tabs under the Clients screen, such as Client Details, Associations, and so on. These tabs are referred to as view tabs. The display within each view tab is called a view. Views provide further details for the particular screen that is in focus.

For instance, if you query for a client on the Clients screen, and then click on the Names view tab, the system will display all names records that exist in GCMS for that client.

Some views also have what are known as applets.

## For instance, in the Background Info view, there is an Additional Family Info applet. Again,

this provides further details for both the screen and view that you have in focus.

You know which screen, view and sub-tab are in focus because the system highlights the words in the tab in black. Notice that there are multiple terms under the Background Info view. These are known as sub-tabs (also, highlight the sub-tabs in GCMS). Sub-tabs are a method of sub dividing and grouping similar information, and can be found on both a screen

## or a view. In the Background Info view, users record different types of background

information, such as family information, travel history, and so forth.

## Tabs

You can use three main tabs to navigate through GCMS. The first is the screen tab. Screen tabs are located just below the GCMS application menu. Each screen tab represents the information component available in GCMS.

The second is the view tab. The view tab is always displayed underneath screens. The view tabs that are displayed differ depending on the screen tab selected.

The third is the sub-tab. Some screen and view tabs have associated sub-tabs. The sub-tabs that are displayed differ depending on the screen or view tab selected.

## Internet Browser

If you are familiar navigating an internet browser, you will notice that GCMS incorporates many of the same features and principles.

### Hyperlinks

Hyperlinks allow you to link directly to another location electronically. Clicking on hyperlinks

#### takes you to the selected item. Hyperlinks are displayed in blue font and become underlined

when you roll your mouse over them.

#### Thread Bar

The thread bar is similar to a history function which lets you retrace your steps in the

#### application. It keeps track of the specific screens and views you have visited while working

in GCMS.

## Production: Issuing Travel Documents Using GCMS

# (CC8218)

#### Course Objective

At the end of this course. you will be able to complete the following activities in GCMS:

- Perform data verification:
- Use the group function to manage several travel document applications to be sent to ePPS;
- Perform Quality Control;
- Print and confirm observations to be added in the travel document;
- Authorize the travel document:
- Generate an address label,
- Record delivery details and confirm the travel document.
This course is divided into two components:

- Finalizing the Application (pre-TD issuance)
- Issuing the Travel Document (post-TD issuance)
Depending on your job function, you will be required to complete one or both of these training components.

Course Content

- Transitioning to GCMS: Overview and Transitioning to GCMS
- Performing Data Verification
- Using the Group Function to Manage Passport Applications to be Sent to ePPS
- Perform Quality Control
- Print and Confirm Observation
- Authorize the Travel Document
- Generate an Address Label
- Record Delivery Details and Confirm Issuance of the Travel Document
- Wrap Up
### Audience

This course is for the passport program operational staff that have or will have responsibilities within GCMS.

#### Delivery Method

- Online and self-paced. The use of CIC's supported browser (Internet Explorer 8) is recommended.
Duration

- 1 hour
Note:

1. The employee should fll out the training form PER 0030E (PDF. 1.5 MB), Training Application and Authorization" and obtain their manager's signature. The manager/employee should send the PER 0030E Training form to the Regional Training Coordinator. Please note also that completing this training during woriing hours requires your manager's approval.
2. The course has accompanying audio narration. You may wish to use a head set to ensure a better learing experience for you and in order to minimize disruptions for your colleagues. A quiet environment, free of distractions is more conducive to learning

## GCMS Orientation Guide

## 16- GCMS Quick Reference Sheet: Clients

Prospective vs. Real Clients Immigration clients can exist in two states, prospective and real. A prospective client record is in a preliminary state, created with minimal data. The data or record can be deleted, and does not get sent to FOSS. Real indicates a

# permanent status and can only be conferred after a search in

GCMS or FOSS has been performed. The data can be modified but not deleted, and is sent to FOSS.

## Citizenship clients are always in a real state.

Unique Client Identifier (UCI)

## A client in GCMS is identified by a Unique Client

Identifier (UCI). A real client created in GCMS will have a

## UCI that contains no more than 10 numeric digits. An IMM

## Prospective client will have a UCI that begins with a T’.

If a client existed in FOSS, and is promoted into GCMS,

## the FOSS ID of the client will be retained as the UCI.

FOSS IDs are 8 digits long and begin with a # other than 8. If a client was created in GCMS, the UCI will begin with an 8. Client Information Client and application/case information are grouped separately in GCMS. This facilitates the sharing of client details across applications. Examples of client information

include: marital status, citizenship, address, travel

## document(s), etc. They can be found on Clients screen and

vicws. Clients vs.

## Parties/Organizations/ Entities GCMS also groups information about clients, parties and

organizations/entities separately. A client is any individual

## who has made an application for a CIC service. A party is

## any individual on whom CIC wishes to keep information (Inviter, Representatives, Guardians, etc). An organization

is a company or group of individuals, such as a law firm,

# educational institution or employer. An entity is not an

## individual or group, but a vessel, aircraft, building, etc. Notes

You can record notes in GCMS against a

## client, application/case, party and

### organization or entity.

For additional GCMS Assistance and Training Materials:

#### What is GCMS?

- The Global Case Management System, or GCMS, is the primary system that IRCC uses to Create, Process and Finalize client applications.
- GCMS is used throughout the Centralized, Domestic and International Networks.
- This connects each office together, allowing for up to the minute communication and information sharing
- This also allows for potential work sharing between office.
i.e. Applications submitted to the Visa Office in New Delhí, can be processed in CPC Vegreville
##### I+1 Canada

Enforce how great it is! Centralized network that is used by all system-> Limitless access to information.

##### Main Tab Bar

Tab bars are your main point of navigation in GCMS. The Main Tab bar appears at the top of the screen, and will remain visible at all times. Depending on what screen in GCMS you are on, there could be up to three sub tab bars

### Types of Applications

- CPC Vegreville currently processes Permanent Resident applications and Temporary Resident applications submitted by both Paper and On-line.
- Paper applications will have a barcode with the application number on the first page of the application.
- On-line, or eApps, are assigned to your GCMS ID

## Going into an Application

#### Querying an Application

From any screen in GCMS, clicking the "IMM" tab will bring you to the screen where you are able to query an application Clicking the "Query" button will create a blank line where you are able to enter information You will need to enter the application number under “App/Case # You can do this by either scanning the barcode on a paper application, pasting a copied application number, or typing it. Pressing "Go" or Enter will then provide a clickable link under

### “App/Case #". Clicking this will take you into your application.

## "Client Search"

To get to the "Search" screen, click the “Go To Search" button in the top left quadrant of the screen from within the application.

- This will bring you to the “Search” tab. All clients and parties associated to the application will appear in the "Search Criteria" box, along with their biographical information.
- To conduct the integrated search, click the “SearchAll"button.
- Once the search is in progress, click the “Refresh" button approximately every 10 seconds until the "Search Status" is "Complete"

# Searching Applications

## Hit List:

- Once your search is complete, scroll down to the "IRCC Integrated Search Hit List
- This will display all client results with similar biographical data to your client.
- The leftmost column will display the percentage of match to the search criteria.
- When searching from an application, you will always get a 99% match
•Ideally, you will only get one UCl result with a 99% match.

- There may also be 99% matches under “T#'s”, or “Temporary IDs”
Once you have determined which UCl is associated to your application, click the row to highlight it.
