### SearchingApplications

#### GCMS History

With your client's UCI highlighted in the Hit List, scroll down to the "Person History" tab. Under this tab, all applications associated to the client UCl will be displayed here.

- This will give you an idea of what your client's history in Canada is.
- What types of applications have been applied for
- When they were applied for
- Which office processed the applications
- Final Decision / Outcome of the application
- If you need to review any relevant information in a previous application, you are able to click into the application from this screen.

Searching Applications Manual Integrated Search

- At times you may be required to conduct a manual search.
- To do this, while on the "Search" Tab, click the “Clear" button above the "Criteria" box. This will clear your current search, and create a blank line for you to enter your search criteria in.
- In order to get the most accurate hit result, use only as much information in your search as needed. i.e:
- Family Name
- Given Name
- DoB
- You may then conduct your search as normal.

ACTIVITYIII CASE: QUERY in GCMS

GCMS is simply a "Big Database" where we store and process applications received through various channels around the world.

As a database, we need to query it in order to get the applications.

What is a Query?

# A Query is simply a request we submit to a database, in our case GCMS.

1. A simple Query in the GCMS training Environment :

Let's say, we want to gquery all the study permits applications approved and that are not assigned to anyone in the Office listed under the GCMS training environment. Usually, we have lot of offices in GCMS, but since we are using the GCMS training environment, we have just one office.

In GCMS, we should change the office first before performing any query like the following for the LOB Mission:

# Summary for above Privacy Guideline Chart:

- When a request is made to change for another person, you need to consider their relationship only within open applications, and closed PRD application within 180 days.
- In an Open application;
- Primary Applicants (PA) can change for themselves as well as Dependents (DEP).
- Dependents can change for themselves as well as PAs.
- A sponsor (SPR), Invițer, or Ço-Sig cannot change for PAs or Dependents and vice versa; they can only changê for themselves.
- PAs, DEPs, and SPRs can change for a minor (under 18 years of age).
- A paid or unpaid representative can change for their client (they must be listed in the application as a representative).
- In a Closed application, no changes can be made unless the secondary request is a minor (under 18 years of age).
- The only exception to this is if there is a closed PRD (closed within 180 days).

# Prospective vs. Real

- Applications
- Created as Prospective first
- Prospective App # begins with 'X'
- Clients
- All clients must be searched before they are made Real
- Prospective Unique Client Identifier (UCI) begins with a ‘T’; Real UCI begins with a number
- Once the application and client(s) are real, users can begin processing and assessing the application.

# Navigating between client and

application

- Navigating from the application to the client
- On the application screen (IMM, CIT or PPT), Clients & Parties view, click the hyperlink in the UCl/Party ID field.
- Navigating from the client to the application
- On the Clients > Associations – Applications & Cases view, click the hyperlink in the App/Case # field.
- Once you have clicked a hyperlink to navigate to the application or client, you can click the thread bar in the top left corner to return to the other screen.

# Primary vs. Secondary Office

## Primary Office

- Responsible for the processing of an application
- Populated when the prospective application is created
### Secondary Office

- Multiple Secondary Offices can be added to the same application Has the same access as the Primary Office and can therefore process all aspects of the application

### Lesson 2: Clients and applications

# Activity 2.1: Create a client and application

Instructions You have been handed a Study Permit application to process in GCMS. You will perform three activities: You have 20 minutes to complete the activity. Please note that you must be logged in with User ID C010101 in GCMS.

A) Search and create a real client You must create the client in GCMS, but before you do so, you have to make sure that this client does not already exist in the system. To do this, you must search for the client using their biodata from the application form (we will go into more detail about searching in GCMS in a later lesson).
1. Click the Search screen tab.
### 2. Click the Integrated sub-tab.

3. Click New.
4. Enter information in the following fields: Family Name = improvise © Record Name: Given Name = improvise Record Name: Gender = improvise again Record Gender: DOB= yes, again! (YYYY/MM/DD) Record DOB: COB = (not Canada) Record COB:
## 5. Click Search.

6. Click Refresh. (Click Refresh a few times until the Search Status changes to 'Complete.'GCMS searches multiple databases during this time.)
7. Review the results in the IRCC Integrated Search Hit List applet to see if the client exists in GCMS.
8. We'll assume that this client does not exist in GCMS. Click New Client at the top. The system creates the new client and takes you to the Clients > Names view. As you can see, your client's real UCl begins with a number. Record your client's UCl here:
9. In the Marita/ Status field, click the icon and select a value.
10. In the Citizenship(s) field, click the icon and select your client's citizenship.
11. In the CoR (Country of Residence) field, click the icon and select a country.
12. Press Ctrl + S on your keyboard to save the information in GCMS.
B) Create a prospective application Now that you have created your client, you can create their Study Permit application. GCMS Orientation Participant Guide I Page 19
2A-2021-12699-000138

eygs iMmgerten Refyoiés

Lesson 2: Clients and applications

1. Click the Associations view tab.
2. Click New.
3. In the Category/Case field, click the icon and select 'SP' and click OK.
4. In the Rec'd/Initiated Date field, select any date.
5. Press Ctrl + S on your keyboard for the system to save the information and create the new prospective application number. As you can see, GCMS has created an application number starting with an 'X’ and an App Status of 'Prospective.'
C) Promote the application to real
1. In the App # field, click the application number hyperlink.
## 2. Enter information about the visa application in the following fields:

- Rec'd Via
- Province of Destination
- Available Funds (CAD)
- Stay/Program-From Date
- Stay/Program-To Date
3. Press Ctrl + S on your keyboard to save the information. Now it is time to promote your application from prospective to real. Once it is real, it wil always exist in GCMS.
4. Scroll back to the top and click Promote Application. The system verifies that all required client and application details have been entered. You'll see the message Create Process is Complete. The prospective application is now real (the App/Case # no longer starts with an 'X', and App Status changes to 'Open'). If there are any client or application details missing, the system will give you an error message indicating which fields still need to be filled.
5. Click OK. Congratulations! You have created a new real client and application in GCMS!

Instructions Using the client and application you just created, you will practise navigating between a client and their application using hyperlinks. You will also use the thread bar at the top left of the screen to take you back to where you were. Also let's practise some naviagtion concepts that were already taught to reinforce where key information is found in the system. You have 7 minutes to complete this activity.

1. From the IMM-TR > Clients & Parties view, click the hyperlink in the UCl/Party ID field to navigate to the client. The system navigates you to the client's record on the Clients screen, where you can access personal information about the client such as the client's address or name information.
2. Click on the Addresses view tab. As you can see, this view is empty because you have not yet added an address for your client. This is where an address would be added. For the purposes of this workshop, we will skip this step.
3. Click on the Documents view tab. The Documents view tab is where you would enter client document information such as foreign travel documents, ID supporting documents, and photos to name a few.
4. Scroll down a bit to see the Attachments applet. This is where you would see scanned copies of a client's documents in GCMS.
5. Now, let's go back to the client's application. Click the App # hyperlink in the thread bar in the top-left portion of the screen. Now we are back on the application! How easy ©.
6. Finally, if you need to go back to the client, click on the Clients & Parties view and click on the UCl hyperlink in the UCI/Party ID field once again.

##### Complex query activity 1

Sometimes you may need to run a query to retrieve a specific list of applications, such as a list of all the open applications in GCMS that were received during a specific period, such as the current year. Let's practice this.

1. On the PPT screen, click the All sub-tab.
#### 2. Click Query.

3. Enter query criteria in the following fields:
4. In the App Status field, select 'Open.'
5. In the Rec'd Date (short for Received Date) field, enter '> 2019/01/01.'Make sure to remove quotation marks. Notice that you used the greater than sign (">") in the date field to indicate to the system to retrieve all applications that were received after January 1st, 2019. Appendix A: Complex Query Operators contains a list of operators that you can use to customize your query.
6. In the Category field, click the icon and select 'Canadian Travel Document' and click Ok.
## 7. Click Go.

How many applications does the system display?

For this scenario, you need to query for all closed Canadian Travel Document applications that belong to your Primary and Secondary Offices and that were received after 2017.

### 4. Enter query criteria in the following fields:

- In the App Status field, select 'Closed.'
- In the Rec'd Date field, enter '> 2017/01/01.'
- In the Category field, click the icon and select 'Canadian Travel Document.'
5. Click Go. How many applications does the system display?

# Housekeeping & Objectives (10 minutes)

INTRODUCTIONS Present yourself to the class and tell them a little about your experience with IRCC. &Then go over the housekeeping rules with participants: HOUSEKEEPING Class hoursHeures de classe Breaks Pauses Lunch Dîner Sick/Late Absence/Retard Phone number for messages Numéro de téléphone pour messages

PRESENTATION Using the PowerPoint presentation GCMS, Privacy, Call Management and SLIDES 1-3 Online Tools and Services Objectives go over the objectives of the module.

OBJECTIFS À la fin de ce module, les participants seront en mesure de: ★ Se connecter et déconnecter du SMGC; ★ D’utiliser les outils de travail en ligne disponible pour SMGC (Aide-mémoire); ★ Compléter des différents types de recherche dans SMGC; De faire la différence entre un ICU, ID du dossier, ID du cas, No Dem/Cas (Ancien et Restructuration) ★ Compléter un changement d'adresse, créer une note ainsi qu'une correspondance reçue; ★ Énumérer les différents outils en ligne et les services offerts aux clients; Énumérer les principes de base de gestion des appels; et ★ Appliquer les connaissances et les habiletés ci-dessus pour naviguer efficacement dans SMGC.

OBJECTIVES At the end of this module, participants will: ★ Be able to log in and out of GCMS; ★Be able to use the working tools available for GCMS (Job-Aids); Be able to complete different types of searches in GCMS; ★ Be able to tell the difference between a UCl number, a file id, a case id, and App/Case # (Legacy and Rebuild) Be able to complete an address change, create a note as well as an incoming correspondence; ★ Be familiar with the various Online Tools and Services available to clients; ★ Be familiar with the basic principles of Call Management; and ★ Be able to apply the knowledge and skills above in order to efficiently navigate in GCMS. Refer Participants to: HELPFUL TERMINOLOGY The Glossary in their participant guide. Go over the following terminology that they will encounter with the various Lines of Business at IRCC. Although some terms are LOB specific, the general navigation concepts and subsequent search exercises that will follow generally apply to all lines of business. Specifics will be discussed during each LOB training.

Unique Client Identifier (UCI) / FOSS ID A unique client identifier generated by GCMS (8 or 10 digits).

A client in GCMS will be designated a UCI: The UCl of a potential client will start with a “T" The UCI of an Express Entry (PR) candidate or International Experience Canada (IEC) will start with “CAN" until they submit an application. FOSS (Field Operation Support System) is the old system used by IRCC. The details of these older files can be found in the “Get FOSS Details"

### Receipt Number – IPRMS (Integrated Payment Revenue Management System)

## Alpha-numeric number associated with a payment receipt. Example:

P000113211

### Payment Number

## This is a number that is created once a case processing centre allocates a

payment. This number will be found on the client's acknowledgement letter (7 digits). Example 1735197

#### Document Number (Document #)

Alpha-numeric number associated with a document. Example : Work Permit : U000010597, Confirmation of Permanent Residence : T110079607

#### Client VS Party

A client is any person who has made an application for a CiC service or who is subject to CIC enforcement action.

## A party is any payer, organization or entity about whom CIC wishes to

### track information. Some examples of various types of parties are:

a payer: person who pays but is not necessarily the client. For example, the parents of a C-14 adoption application. The client is the child, and until the child's case is created, the parents can be

### found through their Party ID. (Identifier number usually starts with the letter P);

a person: lawyer, interpreter hired by the client or person who paid the fees on behalf of a client and who is not included in the application, etc. (Identifier number starts with the letter P);

### an organization: law firm, company, or organization who paid

the fees on behalf of the client (Identifier number starts with the letter 0);

In the Associations View, point out and describe the following columns:

App Status column: this indicates the status of the application. (e.g., open; closed). App Status Reason: this clarifies the reason for status of the application (e.g., approved; refused). Rec'd Date: this is the date the application was received at the processing center/visa office. YCategory: this shows what type of application was submitted (PRD, TRV, VR-ext etc). Fin Dec: this is the final decision. Fin Dec Date: this is the date the final decision was taken. Subcategory: CDA means the determination is being conducted inside Canada; ovs means the determination is being conducted at a visa office.

Ask participants to click on the App/Case# hyperlink in order to access the permanent resident card file. GCMS will then automatically redirect the user to IMm screen > Other, where users will be able to see when the client became a PR, where the application is being processed, when the application was received, as well as the status of the application.

In the 3rd column, agents can also determine the type of PR card that was requested: Original—New PR, or Initial or Replacement

Once the card is produced and sent to the client, the App Status will change to Closed (1st column). Note: GCMS training environment does not allow for PRC files to be closed. Card will say sent.

OVERVIEW Before asking participants to read over the pages referenced above, explain

GUIDELINES In all cases, it is very important that certain guidelines must be respected:

#### Referrals, notes, and comments (for incoming correspondence)

should be in the language most used by the concerned office. VWhen asked to provide a brief description, do ensure however, to include sufficient information in clear, concise, factual manner to ensure understanding of the situation or the response given to a client. VDo not use all capitals, large, bold, underlined or red text, as these formats are generally used to express anger or insistence. VDo not include opinions or comments. VNotes should be added to all applicant files, if applicable.

#### If an action is required on file, it must be taken right after the call

When an authorized third party calls, indicate the name of that person in the Caller's name field of the referral or comments section of the incoming correspondence.

OVERVIEW Explain to participants that similar to a referral, which is an email we send to an office to signal a situation, an incoming correspondence can be used to signal a situation as well. However, this is done directly in GCMS, and no email is required. Also advise participants that a secondary office must be added in cases where we are adding an IC for an office that is not the Primary Office and is not already in the Secondary Office tab.

Important: Incoming correspondences must be added only:

- In the IMM-CIT > Correspondence view;
- once the application is in the system; and
- an office is listed as primary or secondary.
Otherwise, a referral must be sent as there is no place to create an incoming correspondence. (i.e., a VOS application submitted to OSC that does not appear in the system, for which no SV application number was created and that can only be seen in the Clients > Notes view).

Explain that the information that is entered in the fields of an incoming correspondence should be Copy Pasted from the CHD procedures to avoid errors.

VERY IMPORTANT: To ensure IRCC offices are able to search for reports in GCMS that belong to them:

- There must be no space between “For” and “:". Must be “For:"
- There must only be one space between the ":" and "office name".
Allow participants a few minutes to read over the information and answer any questions they may have.

# Access to Information and Privacy (1 hour)

OVERVIEW Explain to agents that in order to provide case specific information they have to be sure they are speaking to the correct person. Since we cannot identify clients in person, agents must use established operational guidelines in order to identify clients over the phone.

In accordance with the Access to Information Act as well as the Privacy Act, explain to participants they may only access GCMS client personal information in order to carry out and accomplish tasks that have been assigned to them by their employer (i.e., IRCC Client Support Centre).

WHAT IS A As per Connexion, a privacy breach is the improper or unauthorized disclosure, PRIVACY access, collection, use, retention or disposal of personal information. They BREACH? may happen within the department or off-site, and could be the result of accidental errors or malicious actions by employees, third parties or intruders.

Access to any other GCMS client personal information, including the agent's own personal information (if available), family, friends, or any other person of public or private interest, is prohibited without appropriate authorization and/or consent from either the person concerned or the agent's employer.

To summarize the introduction, take a few minutes to watch with video, VIDEO available in Connexion: short and informative video on ATIP

REQUESTS FOR Refer participants to: CASE SPECIFIC Training Modules> Access to Information and Privacy > Request for INFORMATION Case Specific Information SMGC, Protections des Renseignements Personnels, Gestion des Appels et Services et Outils En Ligne GCMS, Privacy Protections, Call Management and Online Tools and Services Guide du Formateur/Instructor Guide

To attain a positive client experience, there are four main elements that need to be achieved:

Providing accurate, correct information that answers the client's needs; Offering a service that is courteous, polite, respectful throughout the call; Using an approach that is focused on reassuring the client while maintaining a positive attitude throughout the call; Demonstrating efficiency throughout the call.

Advise participants that the CSC's Quality Team will be coming to the class at some point to explain the entire quality process, the quality grid and introduce them to the Muscle tool. Prepare a flip chart with the following bullet points:

- Who?
- What?
- When? Where? How?

LISTENING following framework of active listening can help manage calls when we do not FRAMEWORK have all the answers:

- Step 1: Acknowledge. Acknowledging the frustration or that this is a difficult time for clients and their families. This is validating to the client.

- Step 2: Apologize: Apologizing in this context would not be admitting fault, rather it expresses empathy toward the client's concern. It would typically follow the acknowledgment statement.

- Step 3: Listen. Letting the client explain their situation and avoiding interruptions demonstrates that we care about their experience, even if we cannot help at the moment. In this step, an agent could use paraphrasing to demonstrate that they care and are trying to understand. Saying something like, "It sounds like you are concerned about XYZ, am I understanding correctly?" demonstrates active listening.

- Step 4: Empathize. This is about demonstrating that we care, even though we may not have the answers. Essentially, it is reassuring and validating the client. An easy way to demonstrate this is to say, "I can see how this is a difficult situation you are facing."

- Step 5: Negotiate. At this point, we have shown that we acknowledge the problem, have apologized for it, and have demonstrated that we understand and care. Now we can try to make a plan forward, even if we don't have all the answers. Because we've laid all the above groundwork to illustrate our commitment to the client, directing them to continue checking the website may be just enough to reassure the client that we are working on a solution for them right now. It is also a good place to lay out any common goals between the agents and clients.

Answer any questions the participants may have, remind them that the Quality team will review this framework with them later in training, when they come to share tips and tricks on call management.

## Client VS Party

A client is any person who has made an application for a CIC service or who is subject to CIC enforcement action.

A party is any payer, organization or entity about whom CIC wishes to track information. Some examples of various types of parties are:

a payer: person who pays but is not necessarily the client. For example, the parents of a C-14 adoption application. The client is the child, and until the child's case is created, the parents can be found through their Party ID. (Identifier number usually starts

Using the training UCI (Tel-Aviv Miriam) go over the following. Y Explain to participants that temporary residence applications appear in GCMS as TRV, SP, SP-ext, WP, WP-ext, TRP under the Associations View.

In the Associations View, point out and describe the following columns: App Status column: this indicates the status of the application. (e.g., open; closed). VApp Status Reason: this clarifies the reason for status of the application (e.g., approved; refused). Rec'd Date: this is the date the application was received at the processing centre/visa office. VCategory: this shows what type of application was submitted (TRV, VR-ext, etc.). Fin Dec: this is the final decision. Fin Dec Date: this is the date the final decision was made. V Subcategory: when applicable, this refers to the sub-category the application was submitted under, for example, a specific type of visa (eTA)

Ask participants to click on the App# hyperlink in order to access the TRV file. GCMS will then automatically redirect the user to IMM screen > TR, where users will be able to see where the application is being processed, when the application was received, as well as the status of the application.

Always verify the Correspondence view > Incoming and Outgoing sub-views to confirm if any letters were sent or received.

- Inform participants that job aids exist, and which to access will vary depending on line of business.
- Take a moment to show them the job aid described in Step 5. Important: Not all information can be shared-Before confirming that a letter was sent to the client, it is important to respect the Mandate Immigration Applications. Also take a moment to explain that BELA letters (Bulk Email and Letter Application), do not appear in GCMS. More and more offices are using BELA.

## DAY 2 – approx. 2 hours

# Call Management (20 minutes)

PRESENTATION Refer participants to: Agent's Corner > Quality Assurance Material [http://cicwebcart/agentCorners/callcentre/coach/toccoach-eng.aspx](http://cicwebcart/agentCorners/callcentre/coach/toccoach-eng.aspx)

To attain a positive client experience, there are four main elements that need to be achieved:

Providing accurate, correct information that answers the client's needs; Offering a service that is courteous, polite, respectful throughout the call; Using an approach that is focused on reassuring the client while maintaining a positive attitude throughout the call; Demonstrating efficiency throughout the call.

Advise participants that the CSC's Quality Team will be coming to the class at some point to explain the entire quality process, the quality grid and introduce them to the Muscle tool. Then during training bay, Quality will provide additional support and practice the questioning, needs validation, presentation of ideas and how to do a conclusion.

Prepare a flip chart with the following bullet points:

- Who?
- What?
- When? Where?
- How?
Briefly explain to the class that a fundamental aspect to understanding a client's needs is through proper questioning by asking the following 5 questions to clients: Who, what, when, where, and how. Also mention the importance of using the hold to verify information, but inform participants that if a client is put on hold for more than 15 minutes, they are sent back to the IVR. It is therefore important to return to our clients in a timely manner.

SMGC, Protections des Renseignements Personnels, Gestion des Appels et Services et Outils En Ligne GCMS, Privacy Protections, Call Management and Online Tools and Services Guide du Formateur/Instructor Guide

### Go over the following role play scenario:

Agent: May I have your name (WHO)? John Brown

### Mr. Brown contacts the CSC as he would like to know the status of their

application.

Agent: WHAT type of application did you submit? PR Cord This will confirm the business line.

Agent: WHEN was the application submitted? November 1, 2015

### This will establish a timeline to be measured against the current

processing times.

Agent: WHERE did you apply? PRC Sydney This will confirm the office where the application was submitted.

Agent: How did you apply? Registered mail

This will confirm the method used to apply (NoTE: this question could refer to the method of application—online vs. Paper, OR method of delivery—regular vs. Registered mail)

Once you have gone over the scenario, answer any questions participants may have on this call handling approach.

## ACTIVE Remind participants that some calls will be more challenging than others. The

LISTENING following framework of active listening can help manage calls when we do not FRAMEWORKhave all the answers:

- Step 1: Acknowledge. Acknowledging the frustration or that this is a difficult time for clients and their families. This is validating to the client.

- Step 2: Apologize: Apologizing in this context would not be admitting fault, rather it expresses empathy toward the client's concern. It would

SMGC, Protections des Renseignements Personnels, Gestion des Appels et Services et Outils En Ligne GCMS, Privacy Protections, Call Management and Online Tools and Services Guide du Formateur/Instructor Guide

# Page 94

2A-2021-12699-000286

IdmasatanRefyies mmedys

## typically follow the acknowledgment statement.

- Step 3: Listen. Letting the client explain their situation and avoiding interruptions demonstrates that we care about their experience, even if we cannot help at the moment. In this step, an agent could use paraphrasing to demonstrate that they care and are trying to understand. Saying something like, "It sounds like you are concerned about XYZ, am I understanding correctly?" demonstrates active listening.

- Step 4: Empathise. This is about demonstrating that we care, even though we may not have the answers. Essentially, it is reassuring and validating the client. An easy way to demonstrate this is to say, "I can see how this is a difficult situation you are facing."

- Step 5: Negotiate. At this point, we have shown that we acknowledge the problem, have apologized for it, and have demonstrated that we understand and care. Now we can try to make a plan forward, even if we don't have all the answers. Because we've laid all the above groundwork to illustrate our commitment to the client, directing them to continue checking the website may be just enough to reassure the client that we are working on a solution for them right now. It is also a good place to lay out any common goals between the agents and clients.

Answer any questions the participants may have and remind them that the Quality team will review this framework with them later in training, when they come to share tips and tricks on call management.

# Direcves

Afin de s’assurer que soyons tous à l’aise avec la matière présentée, nous avons créé des exercices pour mettre le tout en pratique.

Veuillez accéder aux outils de travail ci-dessous pour compléter les exercices:

★ WebSri ([http://cicwebcart/whatsnew/index-fra.aspx](http://cicwebcart/whatsnew/index-fra.aspx)) ★Site web d`IRCC externe ([http://www.cic.gc.ca/](http://www.cic.gc.ca/)) ★ SMGC Environnement de formation ([https://gcms-training-smgc-formation.apps.ci.gc.ca/](https://gcms-training-smgc-formation.apps.ci.gc.ca/))

Si vous avez besoin de clarifications, faites-nous signe en cours de formation, il nous fera plaisir de vous répondre!

IMPORTANT! Gardez votre travail au travail!

Le transfert de tout contenu de votre boîte de réception, votre calendrier ou vos notes Outlook vers une adresse de courriel privée contrevient nos politiques et pourrait être signalé comme un incident de sécurité informatique.

Si vous souhaitez étudier à la maison, nous vous invitons donc à visiter le site web d’IRCC. Vous pouvez aussi vous envoyer des textes Info-Client ou prendre des notes en classe et amener votre cahier de notes à la maison.

Rappel : Qu'est-ce qu'une atteinte à la vie privée?

IMPORTANT! Keep your work at work! Forwarding anything from your Outlook inbox, calendar or notes to a private email address violates IRCC's policies and could be reported as an IT security incident. Therefore, if you want to study at home, we invite you to visit IRCC's website. You can also email yourself Info-Client texts or take notes during the training and take your notebook home.

## Objectifs du cours

### À la fin de ce module, les participants seront en mesure de:

★ Se connecter et déconnecter du SMGC; ★ D’utiliser les outils de travail en ligne disponible pour SMGC (Aide-mémoire); ★ Compléter des différents types de recherche dans SMGC; De faire la différence entre un ICU, ID du dossier, ID du cas, No Dem/Cas (Ancien et Restructuration);

### ★ Compléter un changement d'adresse, créer une note ainsi qu'une correspondance

reçue; ★ Énumérer les différents outils en ligne et les services offerts aux clients;

### ★ Énumérer les principes de base de gestion des appels; et

★ Appliquer les connaissances et les habiletés ci-dessus pour naviguer efficacement dans SMGC.

# Course Objectives

At the end of this module, participants will be able to:

★ Log in and out of GCMS; ★ Use the working tools available for GCMS (Job-Aids); ★ Complete different types of searches in GCMS; ★ Tell the difference between a UCl number, a file id, a case id, and App/Case # (Legacy and Rebuild); ★ Complete an address change, create a note as well as an incoming correspondence; ★ List the various Online Tools and Services available to clients; List the basic principles of Call Management; and ★ Apply the knowledge and skills above in order to efficiently navigate in GCMS.

## Numéro de paiement

Numéro unique généré par SMGC une fois qu’un paiement est alloué par un centre de traitement. Ce numéro ce trouve dans les accusés de réceptions envoyées aux clients (7 chiffres). Exemple 1735197

### Numéro de document (No doc contrôlé)

Numéro alphanumérique associé à un document. Exemple : Permis de travail : U000010597, Confirmation de résidence permanente : T110079607

## Client vs partie

Un client est toute personne qui a présenté une demande de service d’IRCC ou qui fait l'objet d'une mesure d'exécution de la loi d’IRCC.

Une partie est tout payeur, organisation ou entité au sujet duquel IRCC souhaite faire un suivi de l’information. Quelques exemples de divers types de parties sont :

## un payeur = une personne qui paye mais qui n'est pas nécessairement le client. Par

exemple, les parents d'un enfant adoptif pour une demande C-14. Le client est l'enfant, et jusqu'à ce que le cas de l'enfant soit créé, les parents peuvent être trouvés avec leur ID partie (Numéro d'identificateur commençant habituellement par la lettre P);

une personne = un avocat, un interprète engagé par le client, une personne qui a payé les frais au nom du client et qui n'est pas incluse dans la demande, etc. (Numéro d'identificateur commençant par la lettre P);

A client in GCMS will be designated a UCI:

A party is any payer, organization or entity about whom CIC wishes to track information. Some

# examples of various types of parties are:

a payer: person who pays but is not necessarily the client. For example, the parents of a C-14 adoption application. The client is the child, and until the child's case is created, the

# parents can be found through their Party ID. (Identifier number usually starts with the

letter P);

a person: lawyer, interpreter hired by the client or person who paid the fees on behalf of a client and who is not included in the application, etc. (Identifier number starts with the letter P);

an organization: law firm, company, or organization who paid the fees on behalf of the client (Identifier number starts with the letter O);

an entity: (non-person or non-organization) a vessel (ship), an aircraft or a building (Identifier number starts with the letter E).

Note: Parties with identifier numbers that begin with "8" are the payment receipt details that were

converted from the previous computer application (the Citizenship Registry System or CRS) before September 7, 2004.

## CORRESPONDANCE REÇUE

Le but de cet exercice est de permettre aux participants de pratiquer un

### LE BUT : changement d’adresse, de courriel et numéro de téléphone, l’ajout d’une

note ainsi que la création d’une correspondance reçue dans SMGC.

Pour les exercices suivants vous devez consulter SMGC, DTA et WebSri.

#### DIRECTIVES :

### En utilisant le numéro de demande fournis par votre formateur :

- Accédez à la demande; et
- Suivez les DTA(s) et aide-mémoires afin d'effectuer : le changement d'adresse, de courriel et numéro de
téléphone, et

### la création d’une correspondance reçue et d’une note.

- Une fois que vous avez terminé, veuillez aviser vos formateur(s) afin qu'ils puissent vérifier que vous avez terminé l'exercice correctement.
### DURÉE : 30 minutes

#### Exercices/Outils

CHANGEMENT DTA > CRP > Changement de coordonnées D’ADRESSE -1. Changement d’adresse et/ou de numéro de téléphone > Dossier est NUMÉRO DE au bureau responsable TÉLÉPHONE 2. Changement d’adresse de courriel

Outils et Aide-mémoires > SMGC > Général : Changement d'adresse pour un client Changement d’adresse de courriel

CORRESPONDANCE DTA > Général > Procédure manquante-divers

## Conclusion

#### Ceci conclu notre formation sur SMGC, Protection des Renseignements Personnels, Gestion des

Appels et Services et Outils en Ligne. En espérant qu’elle vous a été utile!

Au début de la session de formation, notre objectif principal était de vous aider à acquérir les connaissances nécessaires afin de répondre aux demandes des clients en leurs fournissant les renseignements pertinents.

Afin d’atteindre cet objectif, nous avons discuté des différents aspects de SMGC, la Protection

#### des Renseignements Personnels, la Gestion des Appels et les Services et Outils en Ligne. Puis

pour intégrer la matière, nous avons mis le tout en pratique à l’aide d’exercices de navigation et de recherches dans le système SMGC et WebSri.

#### Merci beaucoup de votre participation!

# Conclusion

#### This concludes the GCMS, Privacy Protection, Call Management and Online Tools & Services

module. Hopefully it was useful to you!

When we started a few days ago, we had a main objective which was to help you gain the

#### knowledge you need in order to provide your clients with the information they were searching

for.

#### To reach this objective we have discussed the different aspects of GCMS, Privacy Protection,

Call Management and Online Tools & Services. We have learned to put it all in practice by

#### reading files in GCMS and by learning to search for information using WebCart.

Thank you very much for your participation!

#### Aide-mémoire :

### •Obtenir les détails du SSOBL

Cadre de l’écoute active: Etape 1: Reconnaissance. Reconnaitre la frustration du client ou le fait que la situation est frustrante ou difficile pour le client et sa famille. Ceci valide les sentiments du client.

- Étape 2: S’excuser. Dans ce contexte, s’excuser ne veut pas dire admettre une faute mais démontre plutôt de l’empathie envers la préoccupation du client. Cette étape suit SMGC, Protections des Renseignements Personnels, Gestion des Appels et Services et Outils En Ligne GCMS, Privacy Protections, Call Management and Online Tools and Services Guide du Participant/Participant Guide
# Page 39

2A-2021-12699-000346

mmedys iMmgerten Refyoiés

normalement l'étape de la reconnaissance.

- Étape 3: Écouter. Laisser le client expliquer sa situation et éviter les interruptions démontrent que nous nous soucions de leur expérience, même si nous ne pouvons pas l’aider pour l’instant. A cette étape, vous pouvez paraphrasez pour démontrez que vous essayez de comprendre, par exemple dire « Il semble que la situation XYZ vous préoccupe, est-ce que je comprends bien? » démontre que vous écoutez activement.

- Étape 4: Empathie. Démontrer que nous nous soucions d’eux même si nous n’avons pas nécessairement toutes les réponses. Nous rassurons le client en validant ses sentiments. Une manière facile de démontrer ceci est de dire : «Je vois que vous faites face à une situation difficile. ».

- Étape 5: Négocier. A ce point-ci, nous avons reconnu le problème, nous sommes excusés et avons démontré que nous comprenons leur situation et nous nous soucions d’eux. Nous pouvons maintenant essayer de créer un plan pour aller de l’avant, même si nous ne détenons pas toutes les réponses. Comme nous avons déjà établi la base avec les étapes précédentes, diriger le client vers le client vers notre site web pourrait être suffisant pour les rassurer que nous travaillons a une solution pour eux. C’est également un bon moment pour établir des buts communs entre le client et l’agent.

#### Active listening framework:

Step 1: Acknowledge. Acknowledging the frustration or that this is a difficult time for clients and their families. This is validating to the client.

- Step 2: Apologize: Apologizing in this context would not be admitting fault, rather it expresses empathy toward the client's concern. It would typically follow the acknowledgment statement.
- Step 3: Listen. Letting the client explain their situation and avoiding interruptions demonstrates that we care about their experience, even if we cannot help at the moment. In this step, an agent could use paraphrasing to demonstrate that they care and are trying to understand. Saying something like, "It sounds like you are concerned about XYZ, am I understanding correctly?" demonstrates active listening.
- Step 4: Empathise. This is about demonstrating that we care, even though we may not have the answers. Essentially, it is reassuring and validating the client. An easy way to demonstrate this is to say, "I can see how this is a difficult situation you are facing."
- Step 5: Negotiate. At this point, we have shown that we acknowledge the problem, have apologized for it, and have demonstrated that we understand and care. Now we can try to make a plan forward, even if we don't have all the answers. Because we've laid all the above groundwork to illustrate our commitment to the client, directing them to continue checking the website may be just enough to reassure the client that we are working on a solution for them right now. It is also a good place to lay out any common goals between the agents and clients. # INCOMING CORRESPONDENCE AND ADDING SECONDARY OFFICE

Refer participants to: Tools and Job Aids > GCMS > General > GCMS Job Aids > Creating an Incoming Correspondence [http://cicwebcart/workingTools/gcms/creating](http://cicwebcart/workingTools/gcms/creating) flag-eng.aspx

Tools and Job Aids > GCMS > General > Adding a Secondary office [http://cicwebcart.ci.gc.ca/workingTools/gcms/add](http://cicwebcart.ci.gc.ca/workingTools/gcms/add) office-eng.aspx

OVERVIEW Remind participants that similar to a referral, which is an email we send to an office to signal a situation, an incoming correspondence (iC) can be used to signal a situation as well. However, this is done directly in GCMS, and no email is required. A secondary office must be added in cases where we are adding an IC for an office that is not the Primary Office and is not already in the Secondary Office tab.

Important: Incoming correspondences must be added only:

- in the IMM-CIT > Correspondence view;
- once the application is in the system; and
- for an office listed as primary or secondary.
Otherwise, a referral must be sent as there is no place to create an incoming correspondence. (i.e., a VOS application submitted to OSC that does not appear in the system, for which no SV application number was created and that can only be seen in the Clients > Notes view).

Explain that the information that is entered in the fields of an incoming correspondence should be Copy Pasted from the CHD procedures to avoid errors.

VERY IMPORTANT: To ensure IRCC offices are able to search for reports that belong to them in GCMS:

- There must be no space between “For" and “:". Must be “For:"
- There must only be one space between the “:" and “office name".
Allow participants a few minutes to read over the information and answer any questions they may have.

# MESSAGES, NOTES ET COMMENTAIRES — LIGNES DIRECTRICES

Referez les participants au: DTA > Info utile > Operations > Messages, notes et commentaires – lignes directrices [http://cicwebcart/chd/index-fra.aspx](http://cicwebcart/chd/index-fra.aspx)

## APERÇURappelez aux participants qu’il y aura des situations où ils devront prendre

action dans un dossier. Par exemple, envoyer un message, ajouter une note ou créer une correspondance reçue.

LIGNES Dans tous les cas, il est très important de suivre les directives suivantes: DIRECTRICESles messages, les notes et les commentaires (pour les correspondances reçues) devraient être dans la langue la plus courante du bureau concerné. Lorsqu'il vous est demandé de fournir une brève description ou les points pertinents relativement à la situation, soyez bref et précis; Incluez toutefois assez d'information pour assurer une bonne compréhension de la situation ou de la réponse donnée au client. N'utilisez pas les caractères majuscules, de grande taille, gras, soulignés ou en rouge, car ces formats sont généralement utilisés pour exprimer la colère ou de l'insistance. N'insérez pas d'opinions ou de commentaires, seulement les faits. La note devrait être entrée dans le dossier de chaque demandeur, le cas échéant. Si une mesure est requise dans le dossier, elle doit être prise tout de suite après l'appel. Lorsqu'une tierce partie contacte le Centre de soutien à la clientèle, indiquez le nom de cette personne dans le champ Nom de l’appelant.

Donnez aux participants suffisamment de temps pour lire les aide-mémoires listés plus haut et répondez à leurs questions, au besoin.

APERÇURappelez aux participants que semblable aux messages que nous envoyons par courriel à un bureau pour leur signaler une situation, une correspondance reçue (CR) peut également être utilisé pour communiquer de l’information a un bureau. Ceci est toutefois fait directement dans SMGC et aucun courriel n’est requis. Un bureau secondaire doit être ajouté lorsque vous créez une CR pour un bureau qui n’est pas le bureau principal ni un bureau secondaire.

Important: une correspondance reçue doit être ajoutée seulement : • Dans IMM-CIT > vue Correspondance;

- Lorsque la demande est au système; et
- Un bureau est listé 'principal' ou 'secondaire’.
Autrement, un message doit être envoyé car il n’est pas possible de créer la correspondance reçue. Par exemple, une demande de Vérification du Statut qui n’apparait pas encore dans le système, pour laquelle un numéro de demande SV n’a pas été créé et qui peut seulement être vue dans les notes de l’écran Clients. Expliquez que l'information qui est entrée dans les champs d’une correspondance reçue devrait être Copier Coller de la procédure du DTA pour éviter les erreurs.

TRES IMPORTANT: Afin de s’assurer que les bureaux d’IRCC puissent faire les recherches pour les rapports SMGC qui leur sont envoyés:

- ll ne doit y avoir aucun espace entre “For" and “:". Ce doit être “For:"
- Il doit y avoir seulement un espace entre “:" et “office name".

### GCMS Training Environment – General Instructions for Trainers and Training Coordinators

### The GCMS Training Environment is a non-production environment. It allows specific user groups

to train on how to use GCMS. It mimics the functionality of the real GCMS environment but is not connected to any system that exists in the real environment. It does not contain real production data.

## Since this is a non-production environment, the GCMS Team does not provide troubleshooting

support for instances where a user experiences performance issues or functionality issues

### which have been imported from the real production environment and that users also

experience in the real GCMS system.

#### User Access

To access the GCMS training environment, users must copy/paste this link in Chrome: [https://gcms-training-smgc-formation.apps.ci.gc.ca/,select](https://gcms-training-smgc-formation.apps.ci.gc.ca/,select) their language of preference, and then enter their assigned User ID.

Access to the monthly password can be obtained from the Training Coordinator (IRCC.TrainingCoordination-CoordinationdelaFormation.IRCC@cic.gc.ca). All users share the same password.

The training environment undergoes maintenance work and a Release every month to update it to the most current functionality that exists in the production environment. The general

## L'environnement de formation du SMGC-Instructions générales pour les formateurs et les

coordinateurs de formation

## L’environnement de formation du SMGC n’est pas un environnement de production. Il s’agit

d’un environnement qui a été créé pour permettre à des groupes d’utilisateurs donnés d’apprendre à utiliser SMGC. Il reproduit des fonctionnalités disponibles dans le véritable environnement du SMGC mais il n’est lié à aucun système existant dans le véritable environnement. Il ne renferme pas non plus de données de production réelles.

Puisqu’il ne s’agit pas d’un environnement de production, l’équipe du SMGC ne fournit pas de service de dépannage aux utilisateurs qui sont confrontés à des problèmes liés à la performance du système ou aux fonctionnalités qui ont été importés de l’environnement de production du SMGC et auxquels les utilisateurs sont également confrontés dans ce dernier.

#### Accès de l’utilisateur

### Afin d’accéder à l’environnement de formation du SMCG, les utilisateurs doivent copie/collez le

lien suivant dans Chrome, [https://gcms-training-smgc-formation.apps.ci.gc.ca/](https://gcms-training-smgc-formation.apps.ci.gc.ca/), sélectionner leur langue de préférence et ensuite inscrire l’ID utilisateur qui leur a été assigné.

### ID utilisateurs disponibles pour les formations du Centre

(Note: chaque ID peut être utilisé par plus d’un utilisateur à la fois):

L’accès à l’environnement est contrôlé par des changements de mot de passe mensuels. Chaque mois, l’équipe du SMGC change le mot de passe de l’environnement et envoie ce nouveau mot de passe aux directions générales inscrites. L’accès au mot de passe mensuel peut être obtenu en communiquant avec le coordonnateur de formation (IRCC.TrainingCoordination-CoordinationdelaFormation.IRCC@cic.gc.ca). Tous les utilisateurs

### utilisent le même mot de passe.

## Entretien du système

L’environnement de formation fait l’objet de travaux d’entretien et d’une mise à jour chaque mois afin de reproduire les plus récentes fonctionnalités existantes dans l’environnement de production. De façon générale, les interruptions de services ont lieu les troisièmes mardis et mercredis du mois. Il peut toutefois arriver qu’elles aient lieu à des moments différents.

Vous pouvez obtenir les dates d’entretien du système en communiquant avec le coordinateur de formation (IRCC.TrainingCoordination-CoordinationdelaFormation.IRCC@cic.gc.ca). Les utilisateurs peuvent aussi vérifier les plus récentes dates d’entretien dans l’environnement de formation sous Accueil – Mes messages, immédiatement après s’être connectés (voir tableau ci-dessous).

# Protection des Renseignements Personnels

# Privacy Protection

- IMM5475 : Permet à une personne autorisée d'obtenir de l'information sur le dossier général du client mais ne permet pas d'initier des actions (à l'exception d'un changement d'adresse).
- IMM5476 : Permet à une personne autorisée (rémunérée ou non) d'obtenir des renseignements et d'agir au nom de la personne.
- IMM5475: Allows an authorized party to obtain information on the client's general file but not to take action on behalf of the client (except for à change of address).
- IMM5476: Ällows a appointed party (paid or not) to obtain information and act on the client's behalf.

Notice to Trainers

Your expertise and collaboration as a Trainer is extremely appreciated. You contribute to the success of training at IRCC, in this era of constant change and modernisation.

The Training Design and Development Unit (TDDU) of the Learning and Development Division (LDD) is responsible for the Development & Maintenance of course material for most Operational business lines at IRCC. As we have knowledge and skills mainly in Training designs area, we rely on the business owners to validate accuracy of content and to inform us of any operational changes that could impact our training material.

TDDU is constantly working at updating course content, but in this context of constant change, it has become challenging to keep pace. We know this also has an impact on you the trainers (preparation time and course delivery). In order to assist both training and TDDU the following tools are being implemented to help communicate upcoming changes as well as any unidentified errors in content.

Table 1 below is a way to provide support to you, the trainer, during your preparation

phase. It should also facilitate coordination between TDDU, LPDU and the facilitators when questions are raised regarding course content. You will find in table 1 general notes applicable to all lines of business as well as notes specific to the course, if applicable.

Table 2 below: In case we missed anything, or are unaware of other recent changes in

the field, we need your support and expertise to make us aware. Please signal any errors in content in the table below and transmit it to IRCC.CECSCContinuousLearning- ApprentissagecontinuCSCEC.IRCC@cic.gc.ca &caroline.laberge@cic.gc.ca and ensure to put IRCC.TrainingCoordination-CoordinationdelaFormation.IRCC@cic.gc.ca in Cc. We will then ensure appropriate actions are taken in our next round of updates.

1 In regards to the structure changes to Current Curriculum: While the New Curriculum training material for the Client Support Centre is being developed, the existing Current Curriculum training material has undergone the following maintenance/modifications:

- Rest assured that the overall material remains the same and the slight changes in structure that have occurred are to allow flexibility in the training sequence. A GCMS/Privacy/Call Management/Online Services module has been created and is intended as the first training module for all new hires, covering subjects that all participants need to be familiar with, regardless of the LOB they will be trained on first. The LOB IGs all contain an “Online Services Reminder” and “Amendment and VOS Reminder” if not already covered in the IG as specific part of the course/exercise. There is no exam following this first module however participants' knowledge and ability to navigate GCMS will be evaluated within each LOB exam.
2 In regards to Online Services and Call Management: If participants did not start withGCMS/Privacy/Call Management/Online Services module (and instead for example started with PRC/GCMS or CIT/GCMS where Online Services and Call Management were not covered in depth) you may need to refer instead to the GCMS/Privacy/Call Management/Online Services module to cover “Online Services - 45 minutes” and “Call Management – 20 minutes” if applicable. If this is the case, participants should also then complete Activity #4 – Online Services (30 minutes) in the GCMS/Privacy/Call Management/Online Services module.

Popup and Animation / Menu contextuel et animation Overview In the course overview, you learned how to navigate through the course and what the expectations are for your learning. Perform Data Verification This tutorial taught you about the PPT screen in GCMS which allows you to perform the data verification activity.

Perform Quality Control In this tutorial, you learned all about the various GCMS fields in order to perform quality control on all travel documents.

Print and Confirm Observations Added in the Travel Document This tutorial taught you how to properly generate, print and confirm any observations added in the travel document using GCMS.

Authorize the Travel Document This tutorial taught you how to authorize a travel document once the quality control process has been completed.

Generate an Address Label With just a few clicks, you learned how to create address labels in GCMS.

Record Delivery Details and Confirm the Travel Document In this tutorial, you learned how to record all details pertaining to the delivery of the travel document as well as how to confirm in GCMS that it's been issued to the client.

Wrap Up This is our last stop. We are quickly reviewing expectations, what was covered in the course, and set the stage for what's next.

1B: Open the Scanned Application Form to Verify Personal Information

The following are 2 ways that an application can be opened in GCMS:

On the PPT screen, click the Correspondence view tab Click the Incoming sub-tab Highlight the appropriate application form record Scroll down to the Attachments applet In the Name field, click the hyperlink. The system displays a window with the application form OR

On the PPT screen, click the eDocs view tab Refer to the Dacument Sub Type field to locate the application form record In the eDoc # field, click the hyperlink. The system displays a window with the application form

Once the application is open, do the following:

## Compare the Client's Personal Information

On the PPT screen, under the Personalization Details section, compare the following fields to the application form: 0Family Name 0 Given Name(s) 0DOB 0Gender o Place of Birth Country of Birth

# Introduction

### About this training workbook

This training workbook is intended for GCMS users who do not have a lot of

## previous experience working in GCMS. It provides a structured introduction to

GCMS, including hands-on practice using GCMS navigation and search procedures. Review questions and scenarios will help you apply the knowledge you gain during each lesson.

You will need access to the GCMS training environment in order to complete this

## workbook. Your GCMS Manager will ensure this access is set up for you so you

may work through this document.

This workbook is intended for all new GCMS users. Through this workbook, read- only users will be introduced to GCMS. Users with write access who are not that familiar with GCMS will begin their learning here – with other training materials to follow.

NOTE: As indicated throughout the workbook, some exercises apply only to certain user groups. Unless otherwise specified, complete the exercises as presented.

### Workbi-tting Ste GCMS

2A-2021-12699-000633

iMmgerten Refyoiés

tion

### Workbook learning objectives

### After completing this workbook, you will be able to:

- Identify the different areas on the GCMS home page;
- Define GCMS terms;
- Identify GCMS icons and functions;
- Describe and use GCMS screens, views and applets;
- Use GCMS online help;
- Describe and use GCMS navigation tools; and
- Describe and use GCMS search functionality. NOTE: The GCMS quick reference sheet in Appendix A provides an “at a glance" reminder of the topics covered in this training workbook. You are encouraged to use the quick reference sheet during and after this training. How to use this workbook Sequence The first lesson is the foundation for the lessons that follow. Complete the first lesson before attempting the other lessons or exercises. Timing Complete the exercises at your own pace. We have estimated the time that may be needed for each exercise or lesson to help you plan time for training. You may complete this guide over a few days if needed. Online help The GCMS online help is accessible from the training environment and provides step-by-step directions to help you complete this workbook. Lesson 1 contains instructions for accessing the online help.

A GCMS session is inactivated if there has not been any user input for 45 minutes. On any subsequent attempt to use GCMS, you will receive a message that inactivity time has been exceeded (Figure 4), after which you will be logged out.

GCMS screen hierarchy GCMS uses a hierarchy of screens and views to organize and present information (see Figure 8):

- Screens (A) are located at the top of the display.
- Views (B) are located directly below the screens.
- Applets (C) within a view are located at the bottom of the display and are connected to the specific screen or view in focus. Refer to Figure 8 as you review the GCMS definitions below.

A) Screens A screen acts as a first filter on the information, for example:
- The Clients screen displays client information.
- The Search screen displays search information. The naming convention for a screen is the name on the tab plus the word 'screen'. Examples include the Clients screen and the Events screen. Figure 8 (A) displays the IMM-TR screen.
B) Views A view shows additional details about the selected screen. For example, the Clients screen displays information about a client. The view tabs within the Clients screen organize client data into categories, such as the client's addresses, names, and documents. The naming convention for a view begins with the name of the screen that the view is attached to, followed by the name of the view, and then the word 'view'. In Figure 8 (B), the name of the view is IMM-PR > Clients and Parties view.
# C) Applets

## An applet shows additional information about a record contained in a view.

Applets exist only in certain views. An applet can either be a list or a form and it displays specific information for the selected view. For more information about forms and lists, see the next page.

Figure 8 (C) shows the Client Details applet within the IMM-PR > Clients and

Parties view.

# NOTE: When referring to screen captures in GCMS training materials you will see

the combination of a screen, view, and applet referred to as a view. Figure 8 for example, including screen, view and applet, will be referred to as the IMM-PR > Clients and Parties-Client Details view.

## Forms and Lists

The information in screens, views, and applets is presented in either a form or a list. In Figure 9, the information in the screen is organized and displayed as a form and the information in the view is organized and displayed as a list.

In (A), the record entries are displayed as a form, where information is located in various fields. The form provides additional details about a single record.

In (B), information is presented in a list format. Information is located in a series of rows and columns. Each row represents a separate record. You can select a record by clicking anywhere on on the row.

NOTE: If you click on a hyperlink (text that is blue and underlined) in a record, it will navigate you somewhere else.

practice exercises.

## There are various ways to navigate within GCMS. There are six types of

navigation tools:

- Tabs;
- Internet Browser;

The top part of the site map lists the screen tabs. The bottom part lists the screens and their views.

Introduction Navigating Searching GCMS GCMS GS

### Finding Clients in GCMS

A client is a person who has submitted an application for a IRCC service, or who is subject to enforcement action.

There are two ways to search for clients in GCMS. One is by conducting a name search and the other is by conducting a search using a specific identifier such as a Unique Client Identifier (UCI). Use of Identifier search should be limited to retrieving a known client.

## The exercises that follow provide you with an opportunity to practice finding

### clients in GCMS. Remember, you have ready access to the GCMS online help

feature to assist you in completing these exercises.

### Search-Integrated

Integrated search allows users to perform multiple types of searches on one screen. For an integrated search, the only mandatory field to enter information is Family Name, however, users should enter in as much information as they have in

## order to obtain accurate search results. As a best practice, the minimum five fields

## to enter information in for an integrated search are Family Name, Given Name(s),

### Gender, DOB, and COB.

The best method to search for a client when you do not know if the client exists in FOSS/GCMS is to conduct a name search.

## NOTE: Information from both GCMS and FOSS is displayed in a single result. User

access determines who can see FOSS information.

### Exercise 3.2: Search for a client by name

### In this exercise you will search for Alberto Ramirez by name.

1. In the Search-Integrated screen, click New. A highlighted blank record displays. NOTE: The Client/Party field defaults to blank. As a best practice, leave this field blank so that it searches for both clients and parties. NOTE: You may need to scroll to the right in the Search screen in order to view one or more of the fields listed below.
### 2. Enter the search criteria below.

### GCMS Search Views

There are several views accessible from the GCMS Search screen. Person History

- The Person History view displays a listing of GCMS applications associated to the client.
- The FOSS WIP (Work In Progress) view displays a list of FOSS/WIP applications and processes associated to the client.
- The FOSS PRC (Permanent Resident Card) History view displays FOSS PRC history details associated to the client.
- The Medical History view displays the client's medical assessment.
- The CITz Summary Cases view displays clients or parties (Principal Applicants, Dependants, Authorized Representatives, etc.) and Citizenship summary cases, details, and notes associated to the selected record (person).
- The Client Detail view displays the GCMS client details and name records associated to the client.
- The Party Detail view displays the GCMS party details (with name records) associated to the party.
- The FOsS Address History view displays the FOSS address records associated to the client.
- The eDocs view displays electronic documents that are associated to the client.
- The Files view displays details about paper files that were created for an application in FOSS.
- The CBSA Lookouts view displays Lookout information that exists in the CBSA's Interdiction and Border Alerting Service (IBAS).
- The Client Documents view displays all known document records associated to the client (ex. ID documents, travel documents, IRCC-issued documents). NOTE: For additional information about GCMS Search views, click on the relevant view and press Ctrl + H. A window will appear displaying the related online help topic.

### Search for Lost, Stolen or Fraudulent Document (LSFD)

GCMS allows users to perform a search when a document is suspect or has been declared lost, stolen or fraudulent. This search is performed against CBSA's data- bases and is not a search of GCMS.. There are two ways to search for LSFDs in GCMS. One is by conducting a search by document number and the other is by conducting a search by serial number. The steps to search for Lost, Stolen or Fraudulent Documents are described in the

## Search Screen > Searching by IBAS/LSFD section of GCMS online help.

Search by Employment Validation GCMS allows users to search the ESDC (Economic and Social Development Canada) database for employment validation information. There are two ways to search for employment validation records: By conducting a name search; and

- By conducting a search using a specific ESDC file number. The steps to search for employment validation information are described in the Search Screen > Searching by ESDC section of GCMS online help. Search by eDocs GCMS allows all users to search for and view documents which are saved in the e- Storage repository. The steps to search for documents stored in e-Storage using the eDocs sub-tab are described in the Search Screen > Searching by eDocs >To search using eDocs section of GCMS online help.

### Search by CAIPS

CAIPS was the system that was used prior to GCMS to process immigration applications overseas. CAIPS has been decommissioned and is now used as a

## database. Users are able to search for applications and information in CAIPS using GCMS.

The steps to search for applications in CAIPS using the CAIPS sub-tab are

## described in the Search Screen > Searching by CAIPS >To search by CAIPS section

of GCMS online help.

# Search by IBAS/LSFD

IBAS /LSFD (Integrated Border Alerting Service/Lost, Stolen or Fradulent Document) searches allow users to search for immigration lookouts and LSFD documents in FOSS. The search is based on document number and/or serial

## number and the Country of Issue. The searches are executed individually and the

results combined into a single hit list.

### Querying vs. Searching in GCMS

Querying is a different concept in GCMS. Once a person has verified a client's

## identity in the system by performing a search, and has a unique identifier that

belongs to the client, they can query for them instead of searching.

## A query is used to retrieve all records that meet certain criteria. A variety of

queries can be run on a regular basis to manage your inventory, track volumes, or identify applications for follow up. Queries can be run in any GCMS screen. You can also run a query within a view of a particular record.

The steps to initiate queries in GCMS are described in the Queries section of GCMS online help.

# GCMS/eServices -Integrated Search

1. Introduction to Integrated Search Audience: This publication is intended as a tool to assist users in their transition from using the Search-- Person screen to the Search-Integrated screen. For passport users seeking information on the Search-Integrated screen, please refer to the Passport Specific section of the GCMS Online Help.
## What is Integrated Search?

GCMS has introduced a new search function, Integrated Search, to address search requirements related to the upcoming decommissioning of CBSA's FOSS system and the expanded use of automated processes in CIC.

The Integrated search function introduces additional search types and allows for a more extensive and global search drawing from our various Passport and CBSA partner systems. Note: The ability to view search results is restricted based on user role.

Furthermore, additional searches have been incorporated into this new integrated search which will provide new information useful for processing. For example, a travel document search will allow a user to determine if multiple individuals may be reusing a travel document.

Why is an Integrated Search function required? With current GCMS capabilities, all facilitation and enforcement information for a client is contained in GCMS and/or FOSS with shared client identifiers (i.e. UCis). When a user completes a name search in GCMS, the results are combined and shown to the user as one result set. With the decommissioning of FOSS, most enforcement information will be moved to other CBSA systems.

The CBSA system information will not have the same client identifiers and the search results will be scored differently as it will be completed by CBSA systems. This will make the information difficult to match to the GCMS client profiles accessed by CIC GCMS users.

As a response to address this issue, a new GCMS name search has been developed to display the information from multiple sources so that the user continues to have a full picture of the client's history in one glance.

Where is it found in GCMS? The new Integrated Search function is located in the Search-Integrated screen. As of November 4th, it is the default screen when users click on the Go to Search button in an application.

# GCMS/eServices -Integrated Search

### When will it be deployed?

Since Release 8.1 on July 25, 2015 the new Search-Integrated screen has been accessible on the Search screen by all GCMS users. However, currently the Go to Search button in an application continues to direct users to the existing Search-Person screen. Office use of the new search screen will be done in a phased manner in order to minimize impacts to operations and allow the GCMS team to monitor as users begin using the Integrated Search function.

Starting in August 2015, GCMS team has been working with offices to transition users to the Search

- Integrated screen instead of the Search-Person screen when clicking on Go to Search within an application. The Search-Person screen will remain available until all offices have transitioned to using Search-Integrated but will eventually be phased out. Updates: October 30th FOSS was decommissioned and users will be able to synchronize FOSS information into GCMS using the Synchronize Client button in the Client screen. All FOSS information viewed in GCMS is fixed "point-in-time" information which was present at the time of its decommissioning. For more information, refer to the 3 Integrated Search and FOSs Decommissioning section of this document. On November 4th, with Release 8.1.4.2.5, the Search-Person was removed as a separate tab and users are now directed to the Search-Integrated screen.

Once complete, the integrated search displays results in the lower applets of the Search-Integrated screen.

In the Search-Integrated > Summary applet, you will see a list of all Search Types that the system is launching. Each Search Type record indicates the source and the status of the search. In this applet users are able to launch a new individual search by using the Search Type field and the New and Search buttons. Users are not able to launch a new Search Type if one of the same type already exists with a Status is either in 'Progress' or ‘Complete’. Users are able to delete Search Types and

### create a new Search Type, with the exception of the 'CIC Name Search’.

Note: If a search is stuck at In progress' for longer than expected, you may resolve this by

highlighting the summary search record in question and clicking the Refresh button. You may also try to highlight a summary search record sitting at 'In progress' and then click the Delete button. Then, using the New and Search buttons you may re-launch the search. Alternatively, you may create a new record in the Criteria applet with the same search information and then delete the

#### record at 'In progress'.

The Summary applet also contains fields such as # of Records, Request Max Records, and Request Min Score that limit the number of results to be requested from the search source and displayed in the summary. Users can manually modify these values for the specific instance of the search they are launching.

### Finally, the Summary applet also includes a field to indicate the existence of Derogatory

information (Further information on this can be found in Section 3 below) and a Fi/ter field that is not currently in use.

3. Integrated Search and FOSS decommissioning On December 13, 2014, access to FOSS was disabled for all CIC users except OSC (to provide data integrity services) and CBSA. FOSS functionality will be turned off using a phased approach for CBSA users. This process has already begun and currently CBSA users perform a number of activities such as Confirmation of Permanent Residence (COPR), Refugee Claim Intake and executing removal orders in GCMS. GCMS users continue to have the ability to view FOSS information from GCMS Search by using the Get FOsS Details button. Once all remaining functionality and interfaces that connect to partner systems are available in GCMS, the FOSS information and codes will be point in time and will no longer be updated. At that time FOSS will become read-only and GCMS users will only be able to view the information contained in FOSS. Once a user conducts an integrated search the system presents the results of the search based on the query criteria.

New Applets following FOSS Decommissian

Following the FOSS decommissioning, two new applets have been introduced:

CBSA Lookouts Hit List LSFD search

In early November, GCMS will begin communicating with CBSA's Interdiction and Border Alerting Service (IBAS), which will provide important security and lost, stolen or fraudulent document search information to GCMS users. IBAS also connects to multiple systems (TUSCAN, CSIS, etc). Through the GCMS-IBAS interface, GCMS will send information such as PIL Flags (Primary Inspection Line), Enforcement Indicators, and Documents (including Permanent Resident Cards, permits, eTAs, eFoils and associated travel documents) to the IBAS database. This data will be accessible and used by various CBSA systems that are connected to IBAS.

When a user initiates a search on the integrated search screen for a client, GCMS will automatically run a search for all IBAS/LSFD and CBSA Lookout information that exists in IBAS. Any existing information will be displayed in the CBSA Lookouts Hit List and LSFD applet.

## 4. Self-Guided Learning Activity

As the Search-Integrated screen is currently available to users, you may wish to familiarize yourself with this new functionality prior to the upcoming connection of this screen with the Go To

### Search button. To do this, perform the following steps:

1) Identify an application or case that contains biometric and/or travel/supporting id document information and make note of this information for future reference.
#### 2) Navigate to the appropriate application or case. 3) Click Go To Search.

The system currently takes you to the Search-Person screen.

4) Take note of the information in the search criteria fields (Family name, Given name, DOB).
5) Launch the search and take note of the search results.
#### 6) Now, navigate to the Search-Integrated screen.

### 7) Enter all information noted in Steps 1 and 5.

#### 8) Click Search (or Search All).

9) Scroll down to the lower applets to review the integrated search results. Compare the results with what you saw in the Search-Person screen.
