# GCMS/eServices -Integrated Search

5. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Q1. What does the term 'Refer in the Derogatory field in the CiC Hit List applet search results mean? What trigger the "Refer" olert? A1. "Refer" is a flag to a POE CBSA officer at a primary inspection line (PIL) to refer the client to secondary inspection. This message indicates that at least one of the following is true:
At the time FOSS was decommissioned, an inadmissibility report or allowed to leave existed, which continues to impact this value An info-alert used to flag the client exists ( See operational instructions for more info) A GCMS admissibility has failed

The "refer" indicator may not have an impact on an application in process. If you are unsure, authorized users may be able to review additional information in the client history. Complete an integrated search and review the contents of the client's previous history in GCMS in the FOSS details section in the FOSS applet. When the value is 'Refer', the application may need to be referred to a Canada Based Visa / Immigration Officer (CBO) for further review. CBO's should contact their CBSA liaison officer as appropriate.

Q2. Is the information obtained from the Integrated Search the same as the information from the Person Search? A2. Yes, a search performed with the integrated search contains the same information as the Person Search and additional information as well with the introduction of new search types.

Q3. Is the search scoring algorithm the same in Search-Integrated and Search-Person? A3. Although the Search-Integrated screen has a different appearance from its predecessor, Person-Search, the scoring algorithm is identical to the previous functionality and will return the same results displayed in the previous CIC Hit List applet.

The results displayed in the CiC Integrated Search Hit List are based solely on the score results-no additional criterion is applied during this process.

Currently, records that include a greater amount of matched data are displayed in the list in the order the results are returned by the system against other matches at equal score. Thus, the ranking between records of equal scores is dependent of the time it takes for the system to return a given record from various independent databases.

For example, a search may result in 10 name records with a 96% score. Those 10 records are displayed in the order the results are returned. Therefore, a record that could have an associated family name and a given name may show up 10th in the list if this result is returned last by the system, while a record to which only a family name has been associated with the same score may be displayed first in the list if this result was returned faster by the system.

Q4. Why does the integrated search take longer? A4. Under this new search function, there are multiple searches being completed at the same time pulling information from different sources.

# GCMS/eServices -Integrated Search

The GCMS Team has been made aware of several issues related to the Integrated Search functionality currently experienced by GCMS users.

The GCMS User Issues document provides descriptions of any issues brought to the attention of the GCMS team along with user instructions and expected resolution date, if applicable. Please note that resolved issues will be indicated in the Release Notes document.

At this time it has been reported that when either the 'CBSA Lookout Search' type or the 'CIC Name Search' type have been initiated, there have been instances where the Summary applet may indicate that the search Status is complete while no records are displayed in the applets below.

In this situation, a user should click the Refresh button located at the top of the Search-Integrated screen and the results will populate in the appropriate applets. Please note that a user may need to click refresh more than once in order for the results to display.

Q5. I am not obtaining any results from my integrated search. What should I do? A5. If your search is "stuck", i.e. the search Status remains at "In Progress" even after clicking Refresh, then simply create a new search, copy in the information from your initial search and delete the initial search.

If you are looking for information from a particular search, for example the CiC-Name Search, another option available to you is to select this specific search from the applet below, click Search, and run only that Name Search.

This does not “Complete" the original search, which may still remain at “In Progress", but it may allow you to retrieve the specific information you require in order to finalize your application.

Q6. Can I set up my display so that I can go directly to the view tabs relevant to my work? A6. You can set the order of your screen and view tabs and the default tab the system displays on any applet in GCMS. To be able to set your preferences, for example to set the Person History view Tab as your default tab, See GCMS online help: User Preferences>Tab Layout and set the default View flag on the one you prefer. To rearrange the views on your integrated search screen, remember that the tab Type you are looking for is “Integrated”.

Q7. How can I get the system to launch and disploy the Travel ID document Search type? A7. The Travel/Id Document search type will only return results if you have entered a passport or travel document number in the application, or under the Document # field on the Search-

## integrated screen. Once entered, results will automatically populate in the Travel/ID Document applet.

# GCMS/eServices -Integrated Search

Note that the Travel/ID Documents search does not display every passport used by a client as recorded in GCMS. Rather, it serves to indicate if a given travel document or passport has been associated with other UCls.

Q8. Why is the integrated search screen so long? A8. Under this new search function, there are multiple searches being completed at the same time pulling information from different sources. The information displayed allows for enhanced program integrity. In order to give you a fulsome view of all the information available on the client, the system displays an applet for each search type containing detailed results. TIP: Use the right scroll bar or your mouse scroller to navigate up and down through the screen. You may also use the “Expand/Hide" button at the right-top corner of each applet to minimize the applets you don't need for your particular search.

Q9. How can I adjust the number of records returned during a search in the Summary applet? A9. The Summary applet contains fields such as Request Max Records, which limits the total number of records requested from the search source, and Request Min Score which sets the minimum score required for a record to be returned during a search. Users can manually modify these values for the specific instance of the search they are launching. Refer to the training video for more information

Q10. What independent databases are used by GCMS to pull different information? A10. With the decommissioning of FOSS, GCMS becomes the system of record for all FOSS LOBs and for the Interim Federal Health Program (IFHP). GCMS will directly connect with: IRB's NOVA System (GCMS and OSC will recreate any refugee claims that only exist in FOSS on an as-needed basis, when a decision is sent by the IRB); RCMP's CPIC system for the transmission of warrants; GCMS will begin communicating with CBSA's Interdiction and Border Alerting Service

## (IBAS)

Q11 How will I know who has the access levels to view, add or remove derogatory information? A11. Employees who were previously able to view detailed derogatory information in FOSS will continue to be able to do so in GCMS. For example, users with limited access may only be able to view the type of derogatory information (ex: 'Wanted', 'Refer", 'Danger', etc.) information returned under the derogatory field

Q12. Why are there no FOSS Action Codes for some clients? A12. This indicates that the client likely exists only in GCMS and was never recorded in FOSS.

# GCMS/eServices — Integrated Search

Q13. Will the Integrated Search impact the automated decision making? A13. The new Integrated Search functionality has no impact on the Automated Decision making process for lines of business such as the eTA and Express Entry programs. The system- based validation rules for these processes are identical to those in place prior to the introduction of this functionality.

The current known user issues related to the integrated search have been investigated and it has been determined that these issues do not impact the automated decision process such as the Auto Promote or the automated decision-making functionalities.

Q14. Why is there no CBSA Lookouts applet on the Search-Identifier screen? A14. By design, the information from partner databases (including information displayed in the CBSA Lookouts applet) has been integrated and made available in one consolidated location in GCMS. All data about a client drawn from partner databases is consolidated and appears in an integrated manner on the Search -Integrated screen. For any requests to change GCMS functionalities or design, please contact OMC, the Business owners.

Q15. Where can I find the AOC (Associations or Characteristics) field in GCMS? A15. GCMS does not have AOC as it only existed in FOSS but previously stored AOC in FOSS can be found in the Search-Integrated > Client Details applet.

Q17. Is the CBSA Lookouts Hit List linked to the CIC Integrated Search Hit List? A17. No. The information found in the CBSA Lookouts Hit List is taken from an independent database. The information found in that applet might not correspond to the information found in the CIC Integrated Search Hit List. Users should be extremely diligent when scrolling and reading the information provided by ensuring that the client highlighted is the correct client you are searching for. As the two databases are different, a highlighted client in the CiC Integrated Search Hit List might not be the same client highlighted in the CBSA Lookouts Hit List.

Q18. The System no longer displays FOSS Action Codes in the CiC Integrated Search Hit List for clients who are already in GCMS. A18. Starting in Release 9.0.3, all clients that have been promoted into GCMS from FOSS will

## have their information transferred into GCMS and the FOSS Action Codes will no longer appear

in the Search screen. This ensures that users do not refer to outdate/point-in-time information that existed in FOSS before October 30, 2015. To import clients from FOSS please view the Online Help For more information, see To synchronize a client.

Passport Issuance Process Cre ate and capture Application Information This function involves creating a prospective application and inputting the Activity information from the application form including guarantor information, photos and client's preference (date of travel, service type, etc.).

Capture/Update Client Information This function involves creating client information including their address and the

# Activity

2 clients travel document and supporting identification documents. If the client is already in GCMS you will simply be updating their information.

Search This function searches for and matches up a client and their application with Activity 3 existing information in GCMS, the CI and FOSS. This is an important step in establishing whether or not they already exist in the system, which helps establish a clear history of transactions for a client.

Capturing Fees Activity The fees are processed using a different system called IPRMS. Once the fees are processed, you will record the payment in GCMS.

Promote Client and Application At this point, client and application information are considered to be prospective. Activity 5 Authorized users must promote client and application to real before the application can be assessed. Processing of the application can only begin when an application is real. Assess Entitlement The system will conduct these checks by cross referencing information with other Activity 6databases such as the CI. If there is an issue (hits), they will be flagged in GCMS. These issues will have to be reconciled before the application is finalized.

Finalize Application When a finai decision is made (approved, rejected, refused or withdrawn) and if Actraity approved, the travel document is created along with observations, if required. This is used to generate and print the travel document that is later sent to the client.

Print the Travel Document Once the user is satisfied with the print preview, an image of what will appear on page 2 of the travel document, they can send the travel document record for printing through ePPS. Once the travel document is printed and finalized, the Status of the travel document record is updated to 'Authorized' and then Confirmed' in GCMS via an interface to indicate that quality control has been completed and to close the application. Delivery of the Travel Document Acuvity The final stage in the process is to manage the delivery of the travel document. Users are able to record the method and details of the delivery (including the tracking number) in GCMS.

# May6,2015

INTRODUCTION

This lexicon is a job aid designed to facilitate understanding of the vocabulary of Passport Program Modernization Initiative. It is aimed at Passport Program employees of Citizenship and Immigration Canada, Service Canada and those of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development Canada.

### The document contains four sections:

- GCMS
- Modernization
- Passport Program
- Acronyms
This job aid is an evergreen document. The e-Channel team and a sub-working group of the Change Management Working Group created the first version of the lexicon, and CIC-POC is the owner.

Should additions to the lexicon be required:

Service Canada employees: send an email to PPDS-Questions@pptc.gc.ca with the following information: the term to be added, its description and its translation.

Citizenship and Immigration employees, send an email to COP-GS-POC-SM@cic.gc.ca with the following information: the term to be added, its description and its translation.

## PASSPORT PROGRAM MODERNIZATION LEXICON

T DESCRIPTION TERM TERMINOLOGIE TBS-Identity Standard TBS Standard on Identity and Credential Assurance" are: SCT-Gestion de l'identité

(1) TBS Identity Standard-The "Standard on Identity and Credential Assurance" which establishes the requirements for department to adopt a common methodology for assessing their identity and credential risks and for selecting appropriate controls or arrangements to mitigate those risks using a standardized assurance level framework.
(2) Identity assurance level-The level of confidence that an individual, organization or device is who or what it claims to be.
(3) Identity-A reference or designation used to distinguish a unique and particular individual, organization or device.
(4) Trusted referee confirmation-A process that relies on a trusted referee to establish a link to an individual. The trusted referee is determined by program-specific criteria. Examples of trusted referee include guarantor, notary and certified agent.
(5) Supporting evidence of identity-Evidence of identity that corroborates the foundational evidence of identity and assists in linking the identity information to an individual. It may also provide additional information such as a photo, signature or address. Examples include social insurance records; records of entitlement to travel, drive or obtain health insurance; and records of marriage, death or name change originating from a jurisdictional authority.
(6) Foundational evidence of identity-Evidence of identity that establishes core identity information such as given name(s), surname, date of birth, sex and place of birth. Examples include records of birth, immigration or citizenship from an authority with the necessary jurisdiction.
MODERNIZATION

Login Process To log into the GCMS training environment:

1.Launch your Internet browser. Type the following in the address field and press Enter:
2. [https://gcms-training-smgc-formation.apps.ci.gc.ca/](https://gcms-training-smgc-formation.apps.ci.gc.ca/)
3. Click English or Français.
4.Enter your training user ID and password.
5.Click the arrow button or press Enter. Logging out If at any time you need to log out of GCMS, click File > Log
### Out on the Application Menu, or press Ctrl + Shift + X.

NOTE: Do not use the X button on the top-right corner of the browser window, as it will generate user logging errors on the GCMS server.

Timeouts A GCMS session is inactivated if there has not been any user input for 45 minutes.

Closing GCMS Windows After you enter data in a window in GCMS, you should close the window by using the OK or Cancel button, not by clicking the X in the top right-hand corner.

Prospective vs. Real Clients (IMM users) In GCMS, there are two possible states in which clients and applications can reside: Prospective and Real. Applications must always be created as Prospective before being made Real. However, new GCMS clients can be created as Real immediately, as long as a search has been performed

## within 24 hours.

This course will take you approximatety 1 hour to complete.

headset.

Course Structure 2 of 3e So what will you learn today? This course will introduce you to many

concepts about the Global Case Management System (GCMS) which

### you will need to perform your job. This course is intended to provide

you with a general overview and understanding of GCMS and provides a foundation for future training which will focus on specific activities relating to the passport issuance process using GCMS.

### At the end of this course, you will be able to:

- Identify the advantages of GCMS;
- Define common GCMS terms;
- Identify how GCMS supports the Passport Program;
- Understand how to log in and out of GCMS;
- Identify different areas on the GCMS Home page;
- Understand how to use GCMS online help;
- Describe GCMS screens, views, sub-tabs and applets;
- Define GCMS navigation tools;
- Identify GCMS icons and functions.

# What is the Global Case Management System (GCMS)? 1 of 4

The Global Case Management System (GCMS) is the primary system you will use to support many passport functions in the Passport Program. This system will play a key role as the Passport Program moves to modernizing its activities.

The system will support the Passport Program's agenda to improve client services, make better use of resources and enhance the

# integrity of the Passport Program.

Transcript for the Login video Login to GCMS First we'll cover logging in. The steps for logging in are slightly different depending on whether you log in to GCMS directly or via Citrix. Citrix is the secure remote access system that allows users who are outside of the CIC network to access GCMS. Examples include overseas CIC A-2020-24143-000784

2A-2021-12699-000839

### and Citizenship Canadaet Citoyenneté Canada

Information disclosed under the Access to Information Act

users on the Department of Foreign Afairs, Trade and Development DFATD) network and Canadian Border Services Agency (CBSA) users.

When accessing GCMS through Citrix, you must first log into Citrix.

On the Citrix Main page, open the GCMS-SMGC folder.

Then, double click on either the GCMS-SMGC icon to access the English environment or the SMGC-GCMS icon to access the French environment. The icon you choose will determine which language your browser opens in.

Once you double click on an icon, the GCMS splash screen appears. From here, the steps to log into GCMS are the same as when you log into GCMS not through Citrix.

If you are accessing GCMS directly within CIC's network and not through Citrix, you access the production environment URL through the internet browser Chrome. Please note that, if you use Windows 7, you will use the internet browser Internet Explorer.

You are presented with the GCMS splash screen where you can log in with the language of your choice.

Note that the GCMS French and English environments are housed on different servers and you cannot toggle between languages in a session. If you wish to change the language you are working in, you must log out of GCM$ and either open the other icon on the Main page of Citrix or, if accessing GCMS directly, select the other language from the GCMS splash screen, and then log back in.

1. For today's demo, I will click English. The system displays the GCMS login page. Normally, a CIC user enters their CIC email address in the User ID field, and the same password that they use to login to their CIC computer in the Password field. Since this is a non-production environment, I will enter a User ID (C010142) that logs me in as a Port of Spain immigration manager.
2. To login, click the Login arrow.

The GCMS Toolbar Provides access to functions that apply in aíl GCMS screens, and contains drop-down lists and buttons/icons that allow you to navigate.

Displays the GCMS URL, back and forward arrows and Refresh button.

The application Menu Provides access to the following functions: File, Edit, View. Navigate, Query. Tools and Help. and meetings.

The My Homepage area Shows activities that require action on your part, such as My Paused Tasks. My BF (Bring Forward) Activities, My Cases, My Fees, etc.

My Calendar Shows your calendar of GCMS events for the selected date, such as To Dos and meetings.

## Online help

## Now we'll cover the online help.

The online help is context sensitive step-by-step training that is integrated in GCMS.

To access the online help, press Ctrl + H anywhere in GCMS. The system displays a context sensitive online help window. In it, there are hyperlinks to step-by-step instructions for the options that the user has based on the screen that they have in focus. For instance, I have the Administration-User screen in focus, so the online help provides instructions on how to view user access roles.

To access the step-by-step instructions, click the hyperlink. A topic will display with step by step instructions and screenshots.

At anytime, if you want to access online help instructions other than the context-sensitive ones displayed, you can click the Show button in the top left hand corner of the screen to access the table of contents for the online help. The table of contents is organized into two categories; shared and user specific. Anything that is not in Immigration, Enforcement or Citizenship Specific books applies to multiple types of users, whereas, for instance, all of the content in the Enforcement Specific book only applies to CBSA users with Enforcement responsibilities.

Every time there is a GCMS release that changes existing functionality or introduces new functionality which impacts training, the online help is updated as required. A list of all of the new and updated topics is created in the Latest Updates to GCMS Online Help topic for each release.

Finally, there is a helpful search functionality to be aware of which allows users to search based on key words.

# Transcription of video:

Transcript: Anything that is blue and underlined in GCMS is a hyperlink. Clicking on it will navigate you to somewhere else in the system. Right now, I'm on the Home screen, and as you can see, there are multipie applications assigned to me in the My Applications applet.

If I want to navigate to one of these applications, I just click on the hyperlink in the App » field.

The system has navigated me to the IMM screen, PR sub-tab, and I have my permanent resident application in focus

Please take note of the Primary Office and Secondary Office fields, and that the Primary Office field has a value of Port of Spain' while the Secosidary Office field has a value of Mexico'. I will explain the impact of these fields and values when discussing user access.

If I want to see information that is specific to the client on this application, I scroll down, and in the Clients & Partie: view, in the UCI/Party ID field, I click on the hyperlink. The UCI (Unique Client Identifier) is a unique identifer given to an individual clfent, and follows them throughout their interactions with CIC.

The system navigates to the Clients screen, Names view.

In the top left hand corner of the screen, notice that a threadbar has started to appear showing the history of my navigation through the various screens and views. In this instance, it contains the application number that I just navigated from. Another way of returning to the application is to click on the threadbar.

### IRIS® Course Evaluation Guide

You are required to achieve a final mark of 80% or greater in order to successfully complete the IRIS® portion of the Passport Officer training course. # Introduction to IRIS®

The Passport Program network includes a local area network (LAN, also known under the French acronym RL: réseaux locaux) and a

réseau étendu) that allows both desktop data and IRIS® data to be transmitted.

Each office is part of the local area network (LAN) and has a server that links all personal computers and printers in the office and connects personal computers to the wide area network (WAN).

Three major components of the computer network you should be aware of are:

1. Your personal computer
2. The local WIP (work in progress)
- Where the ESRFs being processed are kept.
3. The CI (Central Index) Where all travel document and system lookout files (approximately 9 million files) are kept.

ASCII Codes for Letters with Accents In accordance with Chapter 2 of the Passport Policy Manual (PPM), accents will be included in Canadian travel documents only if they are recognized in one of Canada's official languages, i.e. English or French. The accents found in the list below are the only acceptable French characters to be entered in Passport Canada's travel documents.

Accents must be included in the name and/or place of birth only if the applicant has used accents on the application form. Where the place of birth is the same as any Passport Canada issuing authority, accents must be used (e.g. Montréal).

# Overview of Processing an ESRF in IRIS®

## Notes

1.Launch IRIS®.
2. Create a new ESRF. Press [Alt] + [S], then [N] to select "New" from the Service Request menu and initiate a new ESRF. Using the barcode scanner, enter the service request number and select [OK].
3. Applicant <F2> tab Enter the applicant's personal information.
4. Form <F9> tab Scan the photo card.
5. DEC Data <F3> tab Enter the DEC information and any surname variations. Once the DEC information has been entered, press [Alt] + [Tab] to return to the "Scan Document” window and view the image of the photo. Review the scanned image, crop, then select [OK] in top right corner.
6. Complete the Form <F9> tab Scan the three pages of the application form. Enter the applicant's address(es). Enter the guarantor information. Check the "Data Capture Complete" box.

### 2D Barcodes

Fillable PDF application forms are available to applicants on the Passport page of the Government of Canada website. When applicants fill out the PDF form on line, a 2D barcode appears in the upper right-hand corner of the application form.

This format of the passport application form is available for general applications (adults and children) and simplified renewal applications (adults).

Using the optical scanner, scan the 2D barcode. IRIS® will retrieve the information embedded in the 2D barcode and fill in most of the service request fields.

While the data is being retrieved, if you click on the [Cancel] button, the New Service Request window will reappear.

It is important to wait until retrieval is complete before proceeding with any other data entry (do not touch the keyboard or the mouse).

# Supporting <F4> Tab

Passport officerCourse Reasons for Issuance

The system runs four different queries.

1. Central Index The system queries the Central Index (CI), using primary and secondary data, to see if the applicant already has a travel document. Primary data: *Previous travel document
* Surname
* Date of birth (including phantom date of birth, if applicable) *Surname variations *Date of birth variations *
Secondary data: Given names and initials * Sex

* Place of birth
2. System Lookout-Person The applicant's information is also checked against the System Lookout-Person list on the database.
3. System Lookout-DEC The DEC information that was entered in the DEC Data <F3> tab is checked against the System Lookout-DEC list on the database.

# Referring Security Files to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC)

Since July 2, 2013, the minister ofIm migration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) has been accountable for the issuance of Canadian travel documents and has the sole approval authority on all files that present risks to the Program from the perspective of program integrity, identity fraud and/or passport misuse.

These are some of the more common the files involved:

- An applicant requests a date of birth that is different from the one on his or her documentary of evidence of citizenship; A first-time applicant is unable to provide evidence of citizenship; A custody situation exists that meets existing criteria for a formal risk assessment; Any time there exists uncertainty in custody determination; There is a suspicion of guarantor and/or parental signature fraud; Multiple lost/damaged/mutilated documents; Approval of a second limited validity travel document (LVP) and/or subsequent LVPs (third LVP and over); System Lookout lists: A, AC, R, X, Z; C-41 files.
VStandard remarks are mandatory for all IRCC approvals, which does not prevent Service Canada employees from adding free- form remarks as required in order to properly document the file.

Consult the operational procedures found on our intranet page to learn more about referral to IRCC.

## guarantor verified autom atically, which will produce a report for Operations every

day.

It is important to always understand the reason why a passport is issued to an applicant and how the status of the previous passport is updated in the system.

# IRIS® Processing Data

## Previous passport is still valid

When the applicant has a previous passportthat is still valid and in his or her custody, it must be cancelled in the system. The TD must be marked in the Results <F7> tab. In the Annotate <F11> tab, the reason for issuance should be "Replace Cancelled TD".

Physically cancel the previous passport booklet before giving it back to the applicant, if the applicant requests that it be returned. Add the standard remark indicating whether the TD was returned to the client or destroyed.

3. Previous passport is reported lost or stolen If the previous passport is lost or stolen, that TD must be marked in the Results <F7> tab. In the Annotate <F11> tab, the reason for issuance should be "Replace Stolen TD" or "Replace Lost TD", depending upon the situation. Form PPT 203 must be scanned in the Supporting <F4> tab.
If previous passport was reported lost or stolen without the applicant applying for a new travel document, a hit will appear in the Results <F7> tab. Compare what the applicant reported in the PPTC 201 with what is indicated in the PPTC 203.

The [Lost / Stolen...] button becomes active when "Replace Stolen TD” or "Replace Lost TD" is selected as the reason for issuance. Complete the date and location of the loss/theft as indicated on the PPTC 203.

Note: Service Fees $45 above and beyond the passportfee applies.

## Previous passport is damaged or mutilated

If the previous passport is mutilated or damaged, that TD must be marked in the Results <F7> tab. Choose "Replace Mutilated TD" or Replace Damaged TD" as the reason for issuance.

All mutilated or damaged travel documents must be retained and forwarded to Passport Protection. The duly completed "Declaration concerning a lost, stolen, inaccessible, damaged or found Canadian travel document" (PPTC 203) must be scanned into IRIS®. For all mutilated travel documents, the entire TD must be scanned into IRIS®and the assistant manager must send an email to Passport Protection to inform them that the mutilated travel document is being forwarded to them.

### 7. Previous passport is spoiled

This procedures applies when:

1. There is an error on the bio-data page.
2. There is a defect in the Machine Readable Zone (quality control failure), such as a duplicate stock control number.
3. There is an error related to observations.
4. There is damage to the physical booklet (cover, laminate, binding, etc.) clearly not committed by the applicant, resulting in the travel document being considered faulty. Damaged or mutilated travel documents cannot be replaced under this procedure. In those situations, refer to section 1560 of the PPM. When in doubt, contact your Case Management Analyst (CMA).
## 5. A photo is of dubious quality.

6. The Passport Program mistakenly changed the status.
7. There is express direction from PSDS, Finance or Passport operations senior management (exceptional situations) that has been forwarded to IRCC.
In case of doubt when determining whether the Passport Program is responsible for the error, a supervisor can contact a Data Integrity Analyst (DIA) at IRCC.CNDIFR-IDRFRC.IRCC@cic.gc.ca.

Replacement of a travel document with a faulty chip cannot be performed under this procedure.

Procedure

- Have in hand the travel document to be replaced.

8. Duplicate passport Some foreign nations do not accept Canadian passports containing evidence of earlier visits to countries whose governments they do not recognize. In such cases, Canadian passportholders should obtain a replacement passport. Applications for a duplicate passport must be referred to IRCC for approval.
Consult the operational procedures found on our intranet page to learn more about issuing a replacement travel document.

Following a IRCC recommendation, "duplicate"should not be selected as the reason for issuance when issuing a second valid passport because this automatically changes the status of the previous passport to "held in safekeeping", which is not correct.

By selecting "new" as the reason for issuance, the status of the previous passport stays as "in custody of applicant"and an alert is automatically generated. The alert is then verified by a Data Integrity Analyst (DIA), who ensures that the appropriate IRCC approval has been granted for the duplicate issuance and that the client has provided the necessary information.

The "suspended" status is used when a travel document is suspended in accordance with the Family Orders and Agreements Enforcement Assistance Act. This status is used when the Passport Program has requested the return of the TD, but the TD has not been received.

1. TD status is "suspended": refer the file to IRCC, whether the applicant is on SL-Person or not.
2. Do not mark the TD in IRIS®.
3. Enter remarks in <F11> indicating the TD is on file (indicate all SL hits as per usual).
4. Route the ESRF to security review and refer the file to IRCC.
5. Retain the TD on file pending clearance from the IRCC.
6. Do not physically cancel or mark the TD until advised how to proceed by IRCC.
## 10. PROP

# The "PROP" (pending return of passport) status is used when The Passport Program

requests the return of a TD in accordance with section 11 of the Canadian Passport Order.

1. TD status is "PROP": refer the file to IRCC, whether the applicant is on the SL-Person or not.
2. Do not mark the TD in IRIS®.
3. Enter remarks in <F11> indicating the TD is on file (indicate all SL hits as per usual).
4. Route the ESRF to security review and refer the file to IRCC.
5. Retain the TD on file pending clearance from IRCC.
6. Do not physically cancel or mark the TD until advised how to proceed by IRCC.
11. Revoked The "revoked" status is used when a TD is revoked, either directly or through an adjudication decision. This TD status is used only after the revocation decision has been made. TD status is "revoked": refer the file to IRCC, whether the applicant is on the SL-Person or not. Do not mark the TD in IRIS®. Enter remarks in <F11> indicating the TD is on file (indicate all SL hits as per usual). Routéthe ESRF to security review and refer the file to IRCC. Retain the TD on file pending clearance from IRCC. Do not physically cancel or mark the TD until advised how to proceed by IRCC.

# Limited Validity Passport (LVP)

Issuance of an LVP will be considered only in the following cases: A valid passportis a residency requirement (outside Canada) or The applicant submits proof of imminent travel: o airline, bus, train or boat ticket; travel itinerary that shows proof of payment; o a statement, if travelling by car (validation of the statement is at the

## discretion of the passport officer, e.g. submission of proof of

payment).

Document the file In the Supporting <F4> tab in IRIS®, scan all documentation supporting the LVP application that is not detailed on the passport application form. For example: o Proof of travel; Signed form PPTC 116; Form PPTC 117, wherein IRCC confirms the applicant's Canadian citizenship; IRCC receipt for payment for a new citizenship certificate (Internet receipt); Statement; o All other documentation relevant to the application. Annotate the file to include any pertinent information (remarks).

The decision to issue an LVP to an applicant with an acceptable passport history rests with Service Canada. Issuance of an LVP to an applicant without an acceptable passport history, as well as a second LVP or any subsequent LVP, must be approved by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).

Standard remarks SC

- For a first LVP approved by IRCC: File referred to IRCC for approval For a first LVP approved by SC: 1st LVP approved for issuance due to acceptable passport history For à second or subsequent LVP approved by IRCC: File referred to IRCC for approval
Consult the operational procedures found on our intranet page to learn more about issuing a limited validity passport.

## Passport Care

Multiple incident (MI) files can be detected in three ways:

1. After querying the system, you obtain a hit for an already existing MI file for the applicant.
2. An applicant with an LVP, which was limited because of multiple incidents related to lost, stolen, damaged, mutilated, destroyed by PPTC or found travel documents, is requesting the replacement of that LVP. An OBS 47, RE4 or CE4 is already in the travel document and you obtain an SL hit after querying the system.
3. The CI query results show that a travel document was issued to replace a previous valid travel document that was reported lost, stolen, damaged, mutilated, destroyed by PPTC or found. (You will find that information by looking at the WYSIWYG images of the previous travel document, which also showthe status of the previous travel document.) This replacement travel document is now being reported lost, stolen, damaged, mutilated, destroyed by PPTC or found. This is considered a new MI file, since the replacement travel document is the second travel document reported lost, stolen, damaged, mutilated, destroyed by PPTC or found while still valid and a new MI file will need to be created.
If you determine that it is NOT the same person

1. Add a remark to the file indicating that it is not the same person. If you determine that it is the same person
1. Ensure that the file is properly completed, except for the Annotate <F11> tab.
2. In the Supporting <F4> tab, scan form PPTC 203 completed by the applicant.
3. Obtain proof of travel and scan it the Supporting <F4> tab.
4. Conduct the guarantor check.
5. Document the file (remarks) in the Annotate <F11> tab.
6. Forward the file to IRCC.
7. Add standard remark: "File referred to IRCC for approval"

# IRIS® Renewal

Service Request

## Notes

Once it has been determined that the applicant meets all of the simplified renewal eligibility criteria, the application may be processed.

Due to system limitations, simplified renewal applications must be completed in a specific workflow in IRIS®. When this workflow is not followed, IRIS® does not save the DEC information and any surname variations from the previous file may not be carried over, or may be truncated.

The minimum steps required before saving a file are:

F5 - Enter Stock Control number and run Queries F7 - Select record, mark and accept F2 - Verify there are no truncations in names and place of birth (POB)

- F3 - Retrieve DEC information
After the DEC data has been retrieved in F3, the file can be saved by either going into F12 or closing the file. The user CANNoT enter F12 or close the file prior to entering F3 or the problem will occur.

Processing simplified renewal applications in IRIS®basically involves electronically retrieving information from a previous ESRF to process the new record, without modifying the information.

Except for the specific scenarios outlined in the Eligibility Criteria

## module, passport officers are not to modify the information being

retrieved.

NOTE: Applications submitted with 2D barcodes are to be used with renewal applications, where applicable. When processing an application with a barcode, you must ensure the keyboard language is the same as that of the applicant. You may use ALT-SHIFT to change the language as needed.

Although DEC and ID are not required, if presented, they must be scanned in the appropriate tab.

# Processing Fees

1. Press <F12> to open the Fees <F12> tab.
2. The passport services fee is automatically generated by IRIS®, based on the "Date of Birth", the "Date Received" and "TD Type".
If the "Date Required" is the same day or the next working day after the "Date Received", IRIS® automatically adds the urgent pick-up service fee of $110. ⇒If the "Date Required" is 2 to 9 working days after the "Date Received", IRIS®automatically adds the express pick-up service fee of $50. If pick-up is selected for "Delivery" in the Annotate <F11> tab, IRIS® automatically adds the pick-up fee of $20, unless an Urgent or Express pick-up service fee is automatically generated. ⇒If the reason of issuance is "Replace Lost TD" or "Replace Stolen TD" IRIS generates a $45 fee.

# Call-Back Service Fee

If you select "Call-Back Services" in the "Add Special Fees" window and have not yet accepted payment, then IRIS®corrects any automatically generated urgent or express fee, so that the applicant is not charged the urgent or express pick-up fee on top of the call-back fee.

If payment has already been accepted and then the "Call-Back Services" fee is selected from the "Add Special Fees" window, IRIS® does not automatically correct the urgent or express pick-up service fees that may have been generated.

Correcting the urgent or express pick-up service fees will require the authorization of the manager or team leader. If neither are available to complete the correction, follow local office procedures to reconcile the cash drawer.

Additional information

s.16(1)(c)
Authority to produce certified true copies In the context of this procedure, certification of a Canadian travel document is exclusive to the Passport Program. While other individuals may be authorized to produce certified copies and to charge a fee for that service, e.g. lawyers, members of judiciary, chartered accountants, funeral directors, actuaries, bank managers, this procedure refers to an explicit request that the Canadian travel document be certified by a legitimate Canadian travel document issuing authority. It is the responsibility of the bearer of the travel document to determine the appropriate certifier and to pay the applicable fee.

Passport Program dry seal The Passport Program dry seal is a national security asset classified at the SECRET level, based on the expected injury to the national interest should it be compromised.

Certification authorization The certification of a travel document carries distinct responsibilities; it is therefore important that the manager (or their delegate) perform step 4 indicated in the procedure to underscore that all duties associated with the actual certification of the document are to be carried out by the same individual. This will ensure that the travel document was seen and confirm that any prepared copy is a true copy of the travel document.

Requests submitted by mail to a processing centre may require a call to:

1) Confirm the identity of the applicant.
2) Confirm that the applicant is the person making the request.
3) Confirm the number of copies to be produced.
# 4) Obtain supplementary identification (faxed copies are acceptable).

5) Obtain a signed request PPTC 516.

# Bring Forwards (BFs)

BFs can be used as reminders that pop up each time you enter IRIS®. They can be created when other actions must be taken by the user. The BF can be attached to either a User ID or an ESRF.

Creating a Bring Forward

1. From the Services menu, select Create BF. The Create Bring Forward window appears.
LO Notification Date: 2004-12-09 Use Today's Date: 厂 Assigned To: USER1 Description:

OK Cancel

2. IRIS® automatically prefills the screen with the following information:
- Title bar: User ID and ESRF Number or just the User ID to which the BFs are assigned;
- Notification Date: set at the default number of days after the current date;
- Assigned To: User ID of person creating the BF.
3. You may modify the notification date by typing another date or selecting the "Use Today's Date" option.
4. You may modify the "Assigned To" field by selecting another user from the drop-down list (to assign the BF to another person if you plan to be absent, for example).
5. Enter a short descriptive text (maximum 50 characters) in the "Description" field.
# 6. Enter the details for the Bring Forward in the free-form text

field.

7. Select [OK] or press [Enter] to save the BF.

If you want to open a Bring Forward attached to a particular ESRF, open the ESRF and then select List BF by Folder... from the Services menu. If you want to open a BF attached to a user ID, select List BF by User... from the Services menu.

1. The following is displayed:

Title bar: ESRF number or User ID to which the BFs are assigned; Status: Due or Cleared; SR Number (if applicabie); Notification Date: ordered from the oldest to the most recent; Assigned to: user to whom the BF is assigned; Creator/Last Updater: User ID of the last person to update the BF; Description: summary of the BF (50 characters or less).

Note: If the ESRF is open or the User ID has only one BF attached to it, the
 "Update Bring Forward" window displays immediately, bypassing the "Bring Forward List" shown here.

The Guarantor Did Not Meet One of the Eligibility Criteria:

Main Procedure for Analyzing the Eligibility Report

This procedure describes how the employee of Passport Canada will retrieve and take action on the information provided by the Guarantor Validity and Eligibility Report.

Pre-conditions:

- An Overnight Report has been created and saved on the WIP IRIS® shared drive of each Issuing Authority;
- The selected employees of Passport Canada have printed the Overnight Report.
1. Use the "Applicant information" section of the Guarantor Validity and Eligibility Report to locate all the ESRFs presented on the report.
2. For each ESRF, verify whether a data entry error has occurred in the "TD Number", "Surname" or "Date of Birth" fields. Steps to confirm data:
- Open the ESRF.
- Click on the <F9> tab.
- Click on the "Guarantor" tab.
- Using the image of the form displayed in the window of the "guarantor" section and the content of mandatory fields, compare the information to ensure no error has been made.
3. When no data entry error is detected, confirm the information provided in the "Eligibility" section of the report.
4. If, according to the report, a guarantor has failed to meet one of the eligibility criteria (see below), bring the ESRF back into the "examination" state, open the ESRF and add the remark: "G not eligible: reason". Eligibility criteria:
- Guarantor must hold a Canadian passport valid for five years*.
- Guarantor must hold a valid passport (i.e. a passport whose status is “in custody of applicant", "cancelled" or "replaced by renewal") or one that has been expired for less than one year.

The remark “G eligible: Diplomatic or Special PPT" must be added to the file. To make sure the file does not pass through the eligibility verification process once again, the remark must be added when the file is in the "production" state. To add the remark:

- Open the applicant's ESRF from the "Service Request Query" window;
- Select "Route";
- Click on the "Remark" button;
- Add and save the remark on the file.
2. If the TD number or SCN does not begin with these letters, select "Query" in the toolbar.
3. Select "CI Travel Document" from the list.
# 4.Initiate a query using the TD number in the guarantor's passport.

5. Using the image on the screen, confirm whether the bearer of the travel document is the same as the guarantor in question.
6. If the guarantor cannot be confirmed as the same person as the bearer of the travel document, follow current procedures of escalation.
7. If the travel document has not been extended to its full validity, the guarantor must be refused. A remark stipulating: "G not eligible: LVP not extended" must be added to the file. The applicant must be contacted.
8. If the travel document has been extended to its full validity, close the guarantor's entry in F7. The guarantor can be accepted.
9. A remark stating "G eligible: LVP extended to full validity" must be added to the applicant's file (by following the procedure described in step 1). Before rejecting a guarantor whose TD does not meet the validity period criterion, the Passport Program employee must conduct an additional verification to determine whether the travel document has been extended.

The Guarantor's Travel Document Is a Certificate of Identity, a Refugee Travel Document or a Non-Canadian Diplomatic Passport Currently, the Guarantor Policy only applies to Canadians who hold a Canadian passport. A person who holds a certificate of identity, a refugee travel document or a non-Canadian diplomatic passport cannot act as a guarantor.

When the system has identified that a guarantor does not hold an admissible travel document, the Guarantor Validity and Eligibility Report will confirm the "failed" status under the "TD Type" column of the "Data Validity" section. The passport application must be rejected.

Alternate Procedure for Analyzing the Eligibility Report Alternate procedure to step 3 of the main procedure:

1. When the system indicates that the TD type is wrong, verify the type of travel document held by the guarantor by looking at the "Guarantor" section of the report.
2. Bring the ESRF back into the "examination" state, open the ESRF and add the observation: "G not eligible: reason".
3. Go to F11 and check the "Pending" box.
4. The ESRF is sent to the Guarantor Verification Section, which will call the guarantor and the applicant to convey the pertinent information.

Passport Issuance Process Cre ate and capture Application Information This function involves creating a prospective application and inputting the

# Activity

information from the application form including guarantor information, photos and client's preference (date of travel, service type, etc.).

Capture/Update ClientInformation This function involves creating client information including their address and the

## Activity

2 clients travel document and supporting identification documents. If the client is already in GCMS you will simply be updating their information.

Search This function searches for and matches up a client and their application with Activity 3 existing information in GCMS, the CI and FOSS. This is an important step in establishing whether or not they already exist in the system, which helps establish a clear history of transactions for a client.

Capturing Fees Activity The fees are processed using a different system called IPRMS. Once the fees are processed, you will record the payment in GCMS.

Promote Client and Application At this point, client and application information are considered to be prospective. Activity 5 Authorized users must promote client and application to real before the application can be assessed. Processing of the application can only begin when an application is real. Assess Entitlement The system will conduct these checks by cross referencing information with other Activity 6databases such as the CI. If there is an issue (hits), they will be flagged in GCMS. These issues will have to be reconciled before the application is finalized.

Finalize Application When a finai decision is made (approved, rejected, refused or withdrawn) and if Actraity approved, the travel document is created along with observations, if required. This is used to generate and print the travel document that is later sent to the client.

Print the Travel Document Once the user is satisfied with the print preview, an image of what will appear on page 2 of the travel document, they can send the travel document record for printing through ePPS. Once the travel document is printed and finalized, the Status of the travel document record is updated to Authorized' and then 'Confirmed' in GCMS via an interface to indicate that quality control has been completed and to close the application. Deliv ery of the Travel Document Acuvity The final stage in the process is to manage the delivery of the travel document. Users are able to record the method and details of the delivery (including the tracking number) in GCMS.

# May6,2015

INTRODUCTION

This lexicon is a job aid designed to facilitate understanding of the vocabulary of Passport Program Modernization Initiative. It is aimed at Passport Program employees of Citizenship and Immigration Canada, Service Canada and those of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development Canada.

### The document contains four sections:

- GCMS
- Modernization
- Passport Program
- Acronyms
This job aid is an evergreen document. The e-Channel team and a sub-working group of the Change Management Working Group created the first version of the lexicon, and CIC-POC is the owner.

Should additions to the lexicon be required:

Service Canada employees: send an email to PPDS-Questions@pptc.gc.ca with the following information: the term to be added, its description and its translation.

## Citizenship and Immigration employees, send an email to COP-GS-POC-SM@cic.gc.ca with the following

information: the term to be added, its description and its translation.

T DESCRIPTION TERM TERMINOLOGIE TBS-Identity Standard TBS Standard on Identity and Credential Assurance" are: SCT-Gestion de l'identité

(1) TBS Identity Standard-The "Standard on Identity and Credential Assurance" which establishes the requirements for department to adopt a common methodology for assessing their identity and credential risks and for selecting appropriate controls or arrangements to mitigate those risks using a standardized assurance level framework.
(2) Identity assurance level-The level of confidence that an individual, organization or device is who or what it claims to be.
(3) Identity-A reference or designation used to distinguish a unique and particular individual, organization or device.
(4) Trusted referee confirmation-A process that relies on a trusted referee to establish a link to an individual. The trusted referee is determined by program-specific criteria. Examples of trusted referee include guarantor, notary and certified agent.
(5) Supporting evidence of identity-Evidence of identity that corroborates the foundational evidence of identity and assists in linking the identity information to an individual. It may also provide additional information such as a photo, signature or address. Examples include social insurance records; records of entitlement to travel, drive or obtain health insurance; and records of marriage, death or name change originating from a jurisdictional authority.
(6) Foundational evidence of identity-Evidence of identity that establishes core identity information such as given name(s), surname, date of birth, sex and place of birth. Examples include records of birth, immigration or citizenship from an authority with the necessary jurisdiction.
MODERNIZATION

#### Logging out

If at any time you need to log out of GCMS, click File > Log

## Out on the Application Menu, or press Ctrl + Shift + X.

NOTE: Do not use the X button on the top-right corner of the browser window, as it will generate user logging errors on the GCMS server.

Timeouts A GCMS session is inactivated if there has not been any user input for 45 minutes.

Closing GCMS Windows After you enter data in a window in GCMS, you should close the window by using the OK or Cancel button, not by clicking the X in the top right-hand corner.

Prospective vs. Real Clients (IMM users) In GCMS, there are two possible states in which clients and applications can reside: Prospective and Real. # Introduction

#### About this training workbook

This training workbook is intended for GCMS users who do not have a lot of

### previous experience working in GCMS. It provides a structured introduction to

GCMS, including hands-on practice using GCMS navigation and search procedures. Review questions and scenarios will help you apply the knowledge you gain during each lesson.

You will need access to the GCMS training environment in order to complete this

## workbook. Your GCMS Manager will ensure this access is set up for you, to help

### you work through this document.

Through this workbook, read only users will be introduced to GCMS. Users with write access who are not all that familiar with GCMS will start their learning experience here – with other training materials to follow.

This workbook is intended for all new GCMS users.

NOTE: As indicated throughout this workbook, some exercises apply only to

## certain user groups. Unless otherwise specified, complete the exercises as

presented.

tion

## Workbook learning objectives

After completing this workbook, you will be able to: • Identify the different areas on the GCMS home page;

- Define GCMS terms;
- Identify GCMS icons and functions;
- Describe and use GCMS screens, views and applets;
- Use GCMS online help;
- Describe and use GCMS navigation tools; and
- Describe and use GCMS search functionality. NOTE: The GCMS quick reference sheet in Appendix A provides an “at a glance" reminder of the topics covered in this training workbook. You are encouraged to use the quick reference sheet during and after this training. How to use this workbook Sequence The first lesson is the foundation for the lessons that follow. Complete the first lesson before attempting the other lessons or exercises. Timing Complete the exercises at your own pace. We have estimated the time that may
## be needed for each exercise or lesson to help you plan time for training.

# Online help

The GCMS online help is accessible from the training environment and provides step-by-step directions to help you complete this workbook. Lesson 1 contains

## instructions for accessing online help.

The GCMS home page is the first default screen that many users will see after log in. It provides a snapshot of information specific to each user's account. Your home page displays differently depending on your GCMS user profile and can be customized to meet your specific needs. NOTE: Citizenship users will see the Search screen by default and must click the Home screen tab in order to complete the exercise below.

## Lesson 2: Navigating GCMS

# Introduction

In this lesson you will learn the basics of navigation in GCMS. Using GCMS you wil complete some exercises to apply what you learn.

Learning objectives At the end of this lesson, you will be able to: • Describe GCMS screen hierarchy;

- Identify GCMS navigation tools; and
- Use GCMS navigation tools to explore GCMS. Estimated lesson duration This lesson is expected to take one hour to complete. Lesson 2 intended audiences This lesson is intended for all GCMS users.

### GCMS screen hierarchy

## GCMS uses a hierarchy of screens and views to organize and present information

# (see Figure 8):

- Screens (A) are located at the top of the display.
- Views (B) are located directly below the screens.
- Applets (C) within a view are located at the bottom of the display and are connected to the specific screen or view in focus. Sub-tabs allow information related within a screen or view to be organized in more detailed sections. In the example below, the PR sub-tab is selected within the IMM screen.

Refer to Figure 8 as you review the GCMS definitions below.

A) Screens A screen acts as a first filter on the information, for example:
- The Clients screen displays client information.
- The Search screen displays search information. The naming convention for a screen is the name on the tab plus the word 'screen'. Examples include the Clients screen, and the Events screen. Figure 8 (A) displays the IMM-PR screen.
# B) Views

A view shows additional details about the selected screen. For example, the

## Clients screen displays information about a client. The view tabs within the Clients

screen organize client data into categories, such as the client's addresses, names and documents. The naming convention for a view begins with the name of the screen that the view is attached to, followed by the name of the view, then the word 'view'. In

Figure 8 (B), the name of the view is IMM-PR > Clients and Parties view.

# C) Applets

An applet shows additional information about a record contained in a view. Applets exist only in certain views. An applet can either be a list or a form, and it displays specific information for the

## selected view. For more information about forms and lists, see the next page.

Figure 8 (C) shows the Client Details applet within the IMM-PR > Clients and

Parties view.

# NOTE: When referring to screen captures in GCMS training materials you will see

the combination of a screen, view and applet referred to as a view. Figure 8 for example, including screen, view and applet, will be referred to as the iMM-PR > Clients and Parties-Client Details view.

Forms and Lists

# The information in screens, views and applets is presented in either a form or a

list. In Figure 9, the information in the screen is organized and displayed as a form and the information in the view is organized and displayed as a list. In (A) the record entries are displayed as a form, where information is located in various fields. The form provides additional details about a single record. In (B), information is presented in a list format. Information is located in a series of rows and columns. Each row represents a separate record. You can select a record by clicking anywhere on on the record. NOTE: If you click on a hyperlink (text that is blue and underlined) in a record, it will navigate you somewhere else.

## Navigation tools This section provides a description of GCMS navigation tools, as well as some

practice exercises.

## There are various ways to navigate within GCMS. There are six types of

navigation tools:

- Tabs
- Internet Browser
- Hyperlinks
- Thread bar
- GCMS site map
- Other navigation tools
:Workb-tting Sta--GCMS 2A-2021-12699-001332

# 1. Tabs

Screen tabs are located just below the GCMS application menu. Each screen tab

### represents the information component available in GCMS. Some screen tabs have

## associated sub-screen tabs (see Figure 10).

View tabs are always displayed underneath screens. The view tabs that are

### displayed differ depending on the screen tab selected above.

NOTE: For some screens, in order to access the associated views, a user must click on the ID hyperlink.

You can access a new tab by clicking on it. The color of the tab changes to black to

## indicate that it has been selected. When you navigate from screen to screen using

### tabs, you lose the thread, or the data you were working with.

Figure 10 – Tabs

The Tab drop-down arrow provides access Screen tabs provide access to screens. to additional screens.

## Screen sub-tabs provide access to specific

options within screens.

View tabs provide access to views. The view tabs that are displayed differ depending on the screen tab selected and user permissions.

# 3. Hyperlinks

Hyperlinks are displayed in blue font and become underlined when you hover

### your mouse over them. Clicking on hyperlinks takes you to the selected item and

## is the best way to navigate through GCMS.

### Many GCMS identifiers, such as the Unique Client Identifier (UCI), Case ID /

Application ID #, File ID, Event ID, Document ID, or Medical Address ID are hyperlinked to let you navigate quickly and directly to the information associated with these identifiers.

4. Thread bar You can click on any of the text displayed on the thread bar to bring you back to a view you previously visited. Clicking on the Thread Bar (Figure 12) takes you to the displayed path.
Figure 12 – Thread bar
 S Saesk NOTE: To maintain your current thread, always navigate using the view tabs, sub- tabs and hyperlinks.

# 5. GCMS site map

The GCMS site map (Figure 13) displays a list of hyperlinks that direct you to

### specific screens and views. The list of hyperlinks are all of the screens and views

that a specific user has access to. The list varies based on the type of user and their role.

To access the site map, click on the site map icon () on the GCMS toolbar.

The top part of the site map lists the screen tabs. The bottom part lists the screens and their views.

# Field Type Description

### 1. MVG Applet An MVG is a Multi Value Group. This allows you to

record multiple values for one field. The system maintains a history of all values recorded in the field. It is located to the right of the applicable fields.

## 2.Calculator Opens a calculator to assist you with calculating

amounts.

### 3. Check Box Allows you to turn on or off an option when you

check a check box.

4. Calendar Enables you to select a date from a calendar. It is
located to the right of the applicable fields.

## 5. Pick AppletOpens a window to select from a list of values.

### 6.Drop-down List Provides a list of pre-defined values when you click

the drop-down arrow to the right of the field.

### 7. Open TextAllows you to enter text when the field is white.

### Finding Clients in GCMS

A client is a person who has submitted an application for a CIC service, or who is subject to enforcement action.

There are two ways to search for clients in GCMS. One is by conducting a name search and the other is by conducting a search using a specific identifier such as a Unique Client Identifier (UCI). Use of Identifier search should be limited to retrieving a known client.

## The exercises that follow provide you with an opportunity to practice finding

### clients in GCMS. Remember, you have ready access to the GCMS online help

feature to assist you in completing these exercises.

#### Search Person

When conducting a name search, users can search for multiple persons at the same time and can navigate from one result to the next without losing the entered search criteria.

The best method to search for a client when you do not know if the client exists in FOSS/GCMS is to conduct a name search.

NOTE: Information from both GCMS and FOSS is displayed in a single result. User access determines who can see FOSS information.

GCMS Search Views There are several views accessible from the GCMS Search screen. rsn lisstory FO5S VFOSS PRC listoryledasicry Ciu Summary Cases Clent Deul Perty DetalFOSS Addree hisvor éDoeses

- The Person History view displays a listing of GCMS applications associated to the client.
- The FOSS WIP (Work In Progress) view displays a list of FOSS/WIP applications and processes associated to the client.
- The FOSS PRC (Permanent Resident Card) History view displays FOSS PRC history details associated to the client.
- The Medical History view displays the client's medical assessment.
- The Citz Summary Cases view displays clients or parties (Principal Applicants, Dependants, Authorized Representatives, etc.) and Citizenship summary cases, details, and notes associated to the selected record (person).
- The Client Detail view displays the GCMS client details and name records associated to the client.
- The Party Detail view displays the GCMS party details (with name records) associated to the party.
- The FOSS Address History view displays the FOSS address records associated to the client.
- The eDocs view displays electronic documents that are associated to the client.
- The Files view displays details about paper files that were created for an application in FOSS. NOTE: For additional information about GCMS Search views, click on the relevant view and press Ctrl + H. A window will appear displaying the related online help topic.

### Search by Employment Validation

GCMS allows users to search the ESDC (Economic and Social Development Canada) database for employment validation information. There are two ways to search for employment validation records:

- By conducting a name search; and
- By conducting a search using a specific ESDC file number. The steps to search for employment validation information are described in the Search Screen > Searching by ESDC section of GCMS online help.

## Search by eDocs

GCMS allows all users to search for and view documents which are saved in the e- Storage repository.

The steps to search for documents stored in e-Storage using the eDocs sub-tab are described in the Search Screen > Searching by eDocs >To search using eDocs section of GCMS online help.

## Search by CAIPS

CAIPS was the system that was used prior to GCMS to process immigration applications overseas. CAIPS has been decommissioned and is now used as a database. Users are able to search for applications and information in CAlPS using GCMS.

The steps to search for applications in CAIPS using the CAIPS sub-tab are described in the Search Screen > Searching by CAIPS >To search by CAIPS section of GCMS online help.

# Search by IBAS/LSFD

IBAS /LSFD (Integrated Border Alerting Service/Lost, Stolen or Fradulent Document) searches allow users to search for immigration lookouts and LSFD documents in FOSS. The search is based on document number and/or serial

# number and the Country of Issue. The searches are executed individually and the

results combined into a single hit list.

# Querying vs. Searching in GCMS

Querying is a different concept in GCMS. Once a person has verified a client's identity in the system by performing a search, and has a unique identifier that

# belongs to the client, they can query for them instead of searching.

A query is used to retrieve all records that meet certain criteria. A variety of queries can be run on a regular basis to manage your inventory, track volumes or identify applications for follow up. Queries can be run in any GCMS screen. You can also run a query within a view of a particular record.

The steps to initiate queries in GCMS are described in the Queries section of GCMS online help.

Supporting the passport issuance process0 4 a1 4 Click on each activity to learn how GCMS supports the Fassport Program.

Date Moctor (cate_moanearo

Activity 1: Create and capture Application Information This function involves creating a prospective application and inputting the information from the application form including guarantor, photos and client's preference (date of travel, service type, etc.). Activity 2: Capture/Update Client Information This function involves creating client information including their address and the clients travel document and supporting identification documents. If the client is already in GCMS you will simply be updating their information. Activity 3: Search This function searches for and matches up a client and their application with existing information in GCMS, the Central Index (CI) and Field Operations Support System (FOSS). This is an important step in establishing whether or not they already exist in the system, which helps establish a clear historyof transactions for a client. Activity 4: Capturing Fees The fees are processed using a different system called Integrated Payment and Revenue Management System (IPRMS). Once the fees are processed, you will record the payment in GCMS. Activity 5: Promote Client and Application

At this point, client and application information are considered to be prospective. Authorized users must promote client and application to real before the application can be assessed. Processing of the

## application can only begin when an application is real.

### Activity 6: Assess Entitlement

The system will conduct these checks by cross referencing information with other databases such as the CI. If there is an issue (hits), they will be flagged in GCMS. These issues will have to be reconciled before

# the application is finalized.

### Activity 7: Finalize Application

When a final decision is made (approved, rejected, refused or withdrawn) and if approved, the travel document is created along with observations, if required. This is used to generate and print the travel document that is later sent to the client.

### Activity 8: Print the Travel Document

Once the user is satisfied with the print preview, an image of what will appear on page 2 of the travel document, they can send the travel document record for printing through ePPS. Once the travel document is printed and finalized, the Status of the travel document record is updated to 'Authorized' and then 'Confirmed' in GCMS via an interface to indicate that quality control has been completed and

## to close the application.

Activity 9: Delivery of the Travel Document

The final stage in the process is to manage the delivery of the travel document. Users are able to record the method and details of the delivery (including the tracking number) in GCMS.

### Login to GCMS – Transcript:

### First we'll cover logging in.

The steps for logging in are slightly different depending on whether you log in to GCMS directly or via Citrix. Citrix is the secure remote access system that allows users who are outside of the CIC network to access GCMS. Examples include overseas CIC users on the Department of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development (DFATD) network and Canadian Border Services Agency (CBSA) users.

When accessing GCMS through Citrix, you must first log into Citrix.

On the Citrix Main page, open the GCMS-SMGC folder.

Then, double click on either the GCMS-SMGC icon to access the English environment or the SMGC-GCMS icon to access the French environment. The icon you choose will determine

## which language your browser opens in.

Once you double click on an icon, the GCMS splash screen appears. From here, the steps to log into GCMS are the same as when you log into GCMS not through Citrix.

2A-2021-12699-001377

iMmgerten Refyoiés

If you are accessing GCMS directly within CIC's network and not through Citrix, you access the production environment URL through the internet browser Chrome. Please note that, if you use Windows 7, you will use the internet browser Internet Explorer.

You are presented with the GCMS splash screen where you can log in with the language of your choice.

Note that the GCMS French and English environments are housed on different servers and you cannot toggle between languages in a session. If you wish to change the language you are working in, you must log out of GCMS and either open the other icon on the Main page of Citrix or, if accessing GCMS directly, select the other language from the GCMS splash screen, and then log back in.

1. For today's demo, I will click English. The system displays the GCMS login page. Normally, a CIC user enters their CIC email address in the User ID field, and the same password that they use to login to their CIC computer in the Password field. Since this is a non-production environment, I will enter a User ID (Co10142) that logs me in as a Port of Spain immigration manager.
2. To login, click the Login arrow.

Logout from GCMS – Transcript

To log out of GCMS, in the application menu, click File and then select 'Log Out'. Users can also press Ctrl + Shift + X on their keyboard as ashortcut to log out.

It is important thatyou do not click the X button in the top right-hand corner ofyour browser, as the session will not close properly and it will generate user logging errors on the GCMS server.

## Now we'll cover the Home screen.

As you can see, by default, the system displays the Home screen. The Home screen shows different types of items that are assigned to the user.
