## User access – Transcript:

# The GCMS web pages on Connexion, which is CIC's intranet site, contain usefulinformation

# and references that can be accessed by GCMS users and non-users, including information

on user access.

The User Access Requests page includes links on how to obtain or modify a GCMS account, procedures and general information on user access, and descriptions of responsibilities in GCMS.

There are two user access concepts to be aware of; user access in terms of the user's office, and user access in terms of the user's responsibility.

First, I'll talk about the user's office.

The Primary Office and Secondary Office fields have an important impact on who can access an application. There are two types of access in regards to applications and the user's office; write access and read only. Write access means that a user can modify an application, and read only means that a user can query for an application and view it, but cannot make any modifications. Right now, I am logged in as a Port of Spain user, so I will only have write access on applications where the Primary Office or Secondary Office fields

2A-2021-12699-001382

lmmgasatienedyaeesIdmasatanRefyies

have a value of 'Port of Spain'. The primary office has the ability to add multiple offices in the Secondary Office field to give them write access. Please note that the user has to

# transfer the file to change the value in the Primary Office field.

I'm going to refresh my screen back to the IMM-PR screen so that there is no application in focus. Please note that there is one more important navigation function to be aware of. Some screens have what are known as filter drop-downs. This constrains the information that the system will query for. In this screen, the default value of 'My Primary Office Application' means that the system will only show applications whose Primary Office has a value of the user's office, so 'Port of Spain' for this user, when they perform a query.

# Now, I'll talk about the user's responsibility.

A user's responsibility will control which screens and views they see, as well as the actions

# that they are able to perform in GCMS. Examples of user responsibilities include managers,

visa officers, and clerks.

To see which screens and views a user has access to based on their responsibility, clíck the Site Map. These are all of the screens and views that this user has access to.

All users have access to the Administration-User screen. This screen allows users to view user access information about any GCMS user.

To access it, click the Administration – User hyperlink, and then click it again.

I'm going to query for the user that I am currently logged in as.

1. Click Query.
# 2. In the User ID field, enter the appropriate value. (C010142)

3. Click Go.
# The system displays all of the user access information for this particular user.

The two most important fields are Responsibility and Position.

The Responsibility field lists all of the user's abilities in terms of their responsibilities. User access responsibilities works like a pyramid; if a user has a manager responsibility, then they have the responsibilities of all users who are below them, such as an officer and a clerk. Also, please note that some users have special administrator responsibilities.

# This user has an 'OSC-Bio' responsibility, which allows them to perform specific tasks

related to biometrics. Usually, in an Multi-Value Group (MVG) field, only the record that is marked as Primary is active. The exception to this rule is for the user's responsibility. Even

# though only the 'Manager' Responsibility has the Primary field selected, the user is able to

perform all of the functions that are associated to the responsibilities on this list.

The Position field relates to the user's office. A user can be associated to multiple offices, and the list is displayed in this field. Please note that only one office position can be active at a time. To change the active office, the user must change their position in the User Preferences screen.

#### Now we'll cover the online help.

The online help is context sensitive step-by-step training that is integrated in GCMS.

To access the online help, press Ctrl + H anywhere in GCMS. The system displays a context sensitive online help window. In it, there are hyperlinks to step-by-step instructions for the options that the user has based on the screen that they have in focus. For instance, I have the Administration-User screen in focus, so the online help provides instructions on how to view user access roles.

To access the step-by-step instructions, click the hyperlink. A topic will display with step by step instructions and screenshots.

ones displayed, you can click the Show button in the top left hand corner of the screen to access the table of contents for the online help. The table of contents is organized into two

Citizenship Specific books applies to multiple types of users, whereas, for instance, all of the content in the Enforcement Specific book only applies to CBSA users with Enforcement responsibilities.

Screen Hierarchy Screen Hierarchy 1 D1 2 Now that you are familiar with some of the key terms and tools vithin GCMS, let's look at how the system is structured. GCMS uses a hierarchy of screens and views to organize and present information. They are as follows: Sub tabs A Screens

Date Mocfied: 2015.05.19

Screens are located at the top of the display. A screen acts as a first filter on the information, for example:

The Clients screen displays client information.

## The Search screen displays search information.

The naming convention for a screen is the name on the tab plus the word `screen'. For example, the Clients screen.

Views are located directly below the screens, and views show additional details about the selected screen. For example, the Clients screen displays information about a client. The view tabs within the Clients screen organize client data into categories, such as the client's address, name and documents.

2A-2021-12699-001385

lmmgasatienedyaeesIMmasatAnRefyies

The naming convention for a view begins with the name of the screen that the view is attached to, followed by the name of the view, then the word 'view'. For example, the Clients > Names view.

Sub tabs are located on certain screens and views, and are a method of subdividing information. For example, the Clients > Documents view has the following sub-tabs; Travel Documents, ID Supporting Documents, CIC Documents, and ID Supporting Documents CIT.

The naming convention for a sub-tab varies depending on whether it is located on a screen or a view. If it is on a screen, it begins with the name of the screen that the sub-tab is attached to, followed by the name of the sub-tab, then the word 'screen'. For example, the IMM – PR screen. If it is on a view, it begins with the name of the screen that the view is attached to, followed by the name of the view, followed by the name of the sub-tab, then the word 'view'.

For example, the Clients > Documents – Travel Documents view.

Applets within a view are located at the bottom of the display and are connected to the specific screen or view infocus. An applet shows additional informationabout a record contained in a view. Applets exist only in certain views.

An applet can either be a list (results from a Search) or a form (Client Details) and it displays specific information for the selected view (or sub-tab if applicable).

## Screen Hierarchy – Transcript

At the top of the screen, there are tabs that look like tabs on a binder. These are called screen tabs. Each screen tab allows the user to access a different screen containing specific types of information, activities or applications. For instance, clicking on the CIT screen tab will allow a user to query for and process a citizenship application, whereas the IMM screen tab will allow a user to query for and process an immigration application.

I'm going to click on the Clients screen tab.

A client refers to an individual person. A key concept of GCMS is that a client must exist in order to create any type of application or activity related to services provided to the client. As you can see, there are tabs under the Clients screen, such as Client Details, Associations, and so on. These tabs are referred to as view tabs. The display within each view tab is called a view. Views provide further details for the particular screen that is in focus.

For instance, if you query for a client on the Clients screen, and then click on the Names view tab, the system will display all names records that exist in GCMS for that client.

Some views also have what are known as applets.

For instance, in the Background Info view, there is an Additional Family Info applet. Again,

# this provides further details for both the screen and view that you have in focus.

You know which screen, view and sub-tab are in focus because the system highlights the words in the tab in black. Notice that there are multiple terms under the Background Info view. These are known as sub-tabs (also, highlight the sub-tabs in GCMS). Sub-tabs are a method of sub dividing and grouping similar information, and can be found on both a screen

# or a view. In the Background Info view, users record different types of background

information, such as family information, travel history, and so forth.

## Tabs

You can use three main tabs to navigate through GCMS. The first is the screen tab. Screen tabs are located just below the GCMS application menu. Each screen tab represents the information component available in GCMS.

The second is the view tab. The view tab is always displayed underneath screens. The view tabs that are displayed differ depending on the screen tab selected.

The third is the sub-tab. Some screen and view tabs have associated sub-tabs. The sub-tabs that are displayed differ depending on the screen or view tab selected.

#### Internet Browser

If you are familiar navigating an internet browser, you will notice that GCMS incorporates many of the same features and principles.

### Hyperlinks

Hyperlinks allow you to link directly to another location electronically. Clicking on hyperlinks

#### takes you to the selected item. Hyperlinks are displayed in blue font and become underlined

when you roll your mouse over them.

#### Thread Bar

The thread bar is similar to a history function which lets you retrace your steps in the

#### application. It keeps track of the specific screens and views you have visited while working

in GCMS.

Please take note of the Primary Office and Secondary Office fields, and that the Primary Office field has a value of 'Port of Spain' while the Secondary Office field has a value of 'Mexico'. I will explain the impact of these fields and values when discussing user access. If I want to see information that is specific to the client on this application, I scroll down, and in the Clients & Parties view, in the UCI/Party ID field, I click on the hyperlink. The UCI (Unique Client Identifier) is a unique identifier given to an individual client, and follows them throughout their interactions with CIC.

The system navigates to the Clients screen, Names view. In the top left hand corner of the screen, notice that a threadbar has started to appear showing the history of my navigation through the various screens and views. ## Production: Issuing Travel Documents Using GCMS

# (CC8218)

### Course Objective

At the end of this course. you will be able to complete the following activities in GCMS:

- Perform data verification
- Use the group function to manage several travel document applications to be sent to ePPS;
- Perform Quality Control;
- Print and confirm observations to be added in the travel document;
- Authorize the travel document:
- Generate an address label;
- Record delivery details and confirm the travel document.
This course is divided into two components:

- Finalizing the Application (pre-TD issuance)
- Issuing the Travel Document (post-TD issuance)
Depending on your job function, you will be required to complete one or both of these training components.

Course Content

- Transitioning to GCMS: Overview and Transitioning to GCMS
- Performing Data Verification
- Using the Group Function to Manage Passport Applications to be Sent to ePPS
- Perform Quality Control
- Print and Confirm Observation
- Authorize the Travel Document
- Generate an Address Label
- Record Delivery Details and Confirm Issuance of the Travel Document
- Wrap Up Audience
This course is for the passport program operational staff that have or will have responsibilities within GCMS.

### Delivery Method

- Online and self-paced. The use of CIC's supported browser (Internet Explorer 8) is recommended.
### Duration

- 1 hour Note:
1. The employee should fill out the training form PER 0030E (PDF, 1.5 MB), Training Application and Authorization" and obtain their manager's signature. The manager/employee should send the PER 0030E Training form to the Regional Training Coordinator. Please note also that completing this training during worling hours requires your manager's approval.
2. The course has accompanying audio narration. You may wish to use a head set to ensure a better learning experience for you and in order to minimize disruptions for your colleagues. A quiet environment, free of distractions is more conducive to learning

Associations – Information associated to the client as indicated in the following sub views

- Applications & Cases – LOB's associated to the client

- Households – Duplicate UCI/FOSS ID's in GCMS
Background Info – Client information as indicated in the following sub views

- Additional Family Info – Clients mother and father personal information (PR only) Education/Personal History – Education and Work history for the last 10 years or 18th birthday (PR only) Affiliations – Organizations (PR Only) Government Positions-Government positions (PR Only) Supplementary Information – Military history (PR Only) Statutory Questions – Questions answered from the TR and PR applications (Criminality, Medical, Refusal to Canada, etc)

GCMS Orientation Guide

16- GCMS Quick Reference Sheet: Clients Prospective vs. Real Clients Immigration clients can exist in two states, prospective and real. A prospective client record is in a preliminary state, created with minimal data. The data or record can be deleted, and does not get sent to FOSS. Real indicates a permanent status and can only be conferred after a search in GCMS or FOSS has been performed. The data can be modified but not deleted, and is sent to FOSS. Citizenship clients are always in a real state. Unique Client Identifier (UCI) A client in GCMS is identified by a Unique Client Identifier (UCI). A real client created in ĠCMS will have a UCI that contains no more than 10 numeric digits. An IMM Prospective client will have a UCI that begins with a T’. If a client existed in FOSS, and is promoted into GCMS, the FOSS ID of the client will be retained as the UCI. FOSS IDs are 8 digits long and begin with a # other than 8. If a client was created in GCMS, the UCI will begin with an 8. Client Information Client and application/case information are grouped separately in GCMS. This facilitates the sharing of client details across applications. Examples of client information include: marital status, citizenship, address, travel document(s), etc. They can be found on Clients screen and vicws. Clients vs. Parties/Organizations/ Entities GCMS also groups information about clients, parties and organizations/entities separately. A client is any individual who has made an application for a CIC service. A party is any individual on whom CIC wishes to keep information (Inviter, Representatives, Guardians, etc). An organization is a company or group of individuals, such as a law firm, educational institution or employer. An entity is not an individual or group, but a vessel, aircraft, building, etc. Notes You can record notes in GCMS against a client, application/case, party and organization or entity.

For additional GCMS Assistance and Training Materials: Refer to [http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/systen/gcms-smgc/index-eng.aspx](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/systen/gcms-smgc/index-eng.aspx)

*Note – There is no firm rule on entering notes, each application will be case by case and you will have to determine when it makes sense to place notes that may provide important information to another officer in future extensions of your client MOST COMMON APPLICATION NOTES

1. Submitted with-Father & Client ID, Mother & Client ID, Sibling & Client ID
2. Study Permit – School Name, Program, Length of Program, Anticipated End Date
3. OCWP – EVN #, School, Program, DIR
4. Reason you issued document shorter than requested (other than expired passport)
5. Initial Entry – example Korean, Japanese, American
6. Reason for extension now different than original reason came to Canada
7. Refusals, Withdrawals, Promoted Rejects that are cancelled or Cancelled documents
8. Requesting info from client via fax while holding application at desk
9. Refer to SDS or SA

Members (Households sub view) – All UCI/FOSS ID's or Party #’s related to the client or party Click “New" (Household # is created) Choose “Type" from drop down (Duplicate Client or Duplicate Party) Click “Add" and “Clients & Parties" window appears Enter UCI/Party ID Click “Go” Click “OK” Repeat process for duplicate client/party

#### What is GCMS?

- The Global Case Management System, or GCMS, is the primary system that IRCC uses to Create, Process and Finalize client applications.
- GCMS is used throughout the Centralized, Domestic and International Networks.
- This connects each office together, allowing for up to the minute communication and information sharing
- This also allows for potential work sharing between office.
- i.e. Applications submitted to the Visa Office in New Delhí, can be processed in CPC Vegreville
#### I Canada

Enforce how great it is!

### Centralized network that is used by all system-> Limitless access to information.

#### Main Tab Bar

Tab bars are your main point of navigation in GCMS. The Main Tab bar appears at the top of the screen, and will remain visible at all times.

- Depending on what screen in GCMS you are on, there could be up to three sub tab bars

### Searching Applications

The first thing you will do when processing an application, is to do a "Client Search" To get to the "Search" screen, click the “Go To Search" button in the top left quadrant of the screen from within the application.

- This will bring you to the “Search” tab. All clients and parties associated to the application will appear in the "Search Criteria" box, along with their biographical information.
- To conduct the integrated search, click the “Search All" button.
- Once the search is in progress, click the “Refresh" button approximately every 10 seconds until the “Search Status" is "Complete"

## Searching Applications

##### Hit List:

- Once your search is complete, scroll down to the "IRCC Integrated Search Hit List
- This will display all client results with similar biographical data to your client.
- The leftmost column will display the percentage of match to the search criteria.
- When searching from an application, you will always get a 99% match
- Ideally, you will only get one UCl result with a 99% match.
- There may also be 99% matches under "T#'s", or "Temporary IDs”
- Once you have determined which UCl is associated to your application, click the row to highlight it.

### SearchingApplications

##### GCMS History

With your client's UCI highlighted in the Hit List, scroll down to the "Person History" tab. Under this tab, all applications associated to the client UCl will be displayed here. This will give you an idea of what your client's history in Canada is.

- What types of applications have been applied for
- When they were applied for
- Which office processed the applications
- Final Decision / Outcome of the application
- If you need to review any relevant information in a previous application, you are able to click into the application from this screen.

### Searching Applications

### Manual Integrated Search

- At times you may be required to conduct a manual search.
- To do this, while on the “Search" Tab, click the “Clear" button above the "Criteria" box. This will clear your current search, and create a blank line for you to enter your search criteria in. In order to get the most accurate hit result, use only as much information in your search as needed. i,e:
- Family Name
- Given Name
- DoB
- You may then conduct your search as normal.

Applicants that are applying to become PRs while outside Canada will receive their COPR at the POE once they have landed in Canada from the CBSA officer. Applicants that are within Canada already (such as TRs) can receive their COPR after appearing at a local IRCC Inland Office and have been examined to become a PR.

ACTIVITY III CASE: QUERY in GCMS

GCMS is simply a "Big Database" where we store and process applications received through various channels around the world.

As a database, we need to query it in order to get the applications.

What is a Query?

A Query is simply a request we submit to a database, in our case GCMS.

1. A simple Query in the GCMS training Environment :

Let's say, we want to guery all the study permits applications approved and that are not assigned to anyone in the Office listed under the GCMS training environment. Usually, we have lot of offices in GCMS, but since we are using the GCMS training environment, we have just one office.

In GCMS, we should change the office first before performing any query like the following for the LOB Mission:

# Summary for above Privacy Guideline Chart:

- When a reques is made to change for another person, you need to consider their relationship only within open applications, and closed PRD application within 180 days.
- In an Open application;
- Primary Applicants (PA) can change for themselves as well as Dependents (DEP).
- Dependents can change for themselves as well as PAs.
- A sponsor (SPR), Invițer, or Ço-Sig cannot change for PAs or Dependents and vice versa; they can only change for themselves.
- PAs, DEPs, and SPRs can change for a minor (under 18 years of age).
- A pąid or unpaid representațiv can change for their client (they must be listed in the application as a representative).
- In a Closed application, no changes can be made unless the secondary request is a minor (under 18 years of age).
- The only exception to this is if there is a closed PRD (closed within 180 days).

# Primary vs. Secondary Office

Primary Office

- Responsible for the processing of an application
- Populated when the prospective application is created Secondary Office
- Multiple Secondary Offices can be added to the same application Has the same access as the Primary Office and can therefore process all aspects of the application
